articles.title_zh: Stock Market Today: Nasdaq Opens Higher; SpaceX Shares Surge on Tesla Deal Talks — Live Updates
articles.content_orig:
SpaceX stock jumped Wednesday after the company reported surging revenue growth in its third quarter, and owner Elon Musk floated a potential SpaceX- Tesla merger.
The space company, which made its debut on the Nasdaq in the biggest initial public offering ever in June, reported third-quarter revenue on Tuesday of $14.6 billion, up 161% from the previous year, and beating LSEG consensus estimates of $12.72 billion.
Meanwhile, its operating income came in at $2.8 billion, with net income of $4.4 billion, after reporting a net loss of $1.05 billion in the same period a year earlier.
On an earnings call, Musk said he's considering a combination with Tesla — which would mark the largest merger in history — and that the boards of both companies have created specific committees to discuss a consolidation.
"I do think there's a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity, and there's a lot to be gained from cooperating," Musk said on the call. Tesla is set to report third-quarter earnings after the closing bell on Wednesday.
Shares of other space stocks, including Rocket Lab , Intuitive Machines and AST SpaceMobile climbed on Wednesday.
SpaceX forecasts first-quarter 2027 revenue between $33 billion and $37 billion, beating the average analyst estimate of $22.2 billion, according to LSEG.
"We delivered another strong quarter in Q3. Revenue grew an impressive 161% year-over-year, fueled by continued momentum in Connectivity and a clear inflection in our Super Intelligence business," SpaceX's chief financial officer, Bret Johnsen, said in the earnings release.
Johnsen pinned the strong results on recurring revenue from its satellite internet business, Starlink , and significant expansion of its Super Intelligence [SI] infrastructure.
The company has dived into artificial intelligence this year, which it's now calling SI. The segment is its largest business unit, with revenue soaring ninefold to $7.56 billion from $813 million in the same quarter last year.
Commentary on computing during the earnings call supported "continued pricing power and shorter payback periods" for AI cloud providers, Truist Securities analysts said in a Tuesday note.
"Despite market concerns relating to financing for AI cloud providers this past week, we believe SpaceX's third-quarter 2026 represents the first data point during the earnings season to support the bull case for AI cloud providers," they added.
They explained that demand appears "insatiable," with SpaceX noting that it could rent out its capacity several times over. The analysts said Coreweave and Nebius are set to benefit and capture demand as "pricing power will more than offset higher rates."
The shares of neoclouds Nebius and Coreweave traded marginally lower, while Iren and Applied Digital climbed in early trading on Wednesday.
— CNBC's Lora Kolodny contributed to this report.
Correction: Bret Johnsen is chief financial officer at SpaceX. An earlier version misspelled his name.

articles.title_zh: DOJ official takes swipe at United Airlines CEO amid backlash over wealth tax proposal
articles.content_orig:
Dagen McDowell slams United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby over his proposal for a national wealth tax and a near-100% inheritance tax. She calls out the double taxation and points to the hypocrisy of the airline's own elite status pricing.
United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby is facing criticism over his support for a national wealth tax and inheritance taxes approaching 100%, with a senior Justice Department official joining the backlash by taking a jab at the airline's service.
Harmeet K. Dhillon, assistant attorney general for the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division, weighed in on the controversy with a post on X about her recent experience flying United.
"The WiFi didn’t work on my last two flights," Dhillon wrote.
Her comment followed Kirby's remarks in a recent interview with The New York Times , in which he warned that growing wealth inequality poses a "danger" to American society.
UNITED CEO SILENT ON $32M COMPENSATION AFTER CALLING WEALTH GAP A ‘DANGER’
Harmeet K. Dhillon speaks at the IAC National Summit 2026 at The Diplomat Beach Resort on January 17, 2026, in Hollywood, Florida.
"We should have a national wealth tax — it won’t work by state because people will just move," Kirby told the Times. "And I think we should have inheritance taxes that get close to 100 percent at some level. I would pay them."
Scott Kirby, chief executive officer at United Airlines Holdings Inc., during a Bloomberg Television interview at Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) in Newark, New Jersey, US, on Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026. (Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty Images / Getty Images)
Kirby's position has also drawn attention to his own compensation. The United CEO received about $32.3 million in total compensation in fiscal year 2025, including salary, stock awards and performance incentives. That was roughly 334 times the $96,670 median employee compensation reported by the airline, according to United's 2026 proxy statement.

Beyond his tax proposals, Kirby also addressed United's pricing practices during the interview, defending the airline's decision to charge passengers more for certain seating options.
"There are some customers who want to sit in a window seat or a better seat, and that costs money to deliver," Kirby said.
A United Airlines Boeing 757 departs from Los Angeles International Airport en route to New York on Sept. 19, 2024, in Los Angeles, California. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images / Getty Images)

His comments prompted criticism from some social media users, with some threatening to stop flying United and others urging Kirby to focus on ticket prices and customer service.
One user wrote that Kirby should focus on "Flight safety, price, timeliness," adding, "How about we start with not charging $500 for basic 2 hour domestic routes?"

articles.title_orig: EXCLUSIVE: EBay to lay off 9% of workforce in push to simplify operations, internal memo shows
articles.title_zh: EXCLUSIVE: EBay to lay off 9% of workforce in push to simplify operations, internal memo shows
articles.content_orig:
EBay will lay off about 9% of its workforce in a move to streamline its operations and focus on its fastest-growing areas, a company spokesperson confirmed to CNBC. The layoffs will affect approximately 1,000 employees.
"As we work to capture the significant opportunity ahead, this step was taken to ensure we continue to operate from a position of strength by aligning our teams and resources with our top strategic priorities," the spokesperson said in a statement.
The company also said it will continue to hire in "priority areas aligned with our strategy." As of the end of 2025, eBay had roughly 12,300 employees.
Reuters first reported the news, citing a memo to staff from CEO Jamie Iannone that read in part, "Our strategy is working."
"Continuing to capture the significant opportunity ahead requires us to make thoughtful choices about where we focus and invest," Iannone said in the memo, seen by Reuters.
This is the second round of layoffs for the online marketplace this year, following a 6% workforce reduction that affected about 800 employees, in February. The company has been steadily shrinking its headcount over recent years at the same time it's ramping up spending on artificial intelligence.
EBay also acquired the used clothing resale platform Depop — a brand with a strong customer base of Gen Z and millennial users — from Etsy earlier this year. The $1.4 billion deal was finalized in July .
Shares of eBay were up approximately 1% Wednesday morning.
— CNBC's Annie Palmer contributed to this report.

ABBOTT PARK, Ill., Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Abbott (NYSE: ABT), the global healthcare leader, today announced its intention to separate its Nutrition business into an independent, publicly traded company that will be a global leader in the rapidly expanding healthy nutrition market with approximately $8.5 billion in annual sales and a portfolio of iconic brands.
"As we continue to shape Abbott for the future, this separation will benefit both companies, setting each one up for maximum success in its respective market," said Robert B. Ford, chairman and chief executive officer, Abbott. "Our Nutrition business has a unique opportunity to capitalize on the growing demand for healthy nutrition, and it will be better positioned as an independent company to more effectively direct its strategic resources across its priorities. At the same time, Abbott's core higher-growth, innovation-driven portfolio of medical devices, diagnostics and established medicines has compelling growth opportunities to improve the health and lives of people around the world."
With different investment identities and requirements, growth profiles, and innovation cycles, both companies will benefit from resource and capital allocation strategies aligned to their distinct business models.
Nutrition: A leading healthy nutrition company The Nutrition company will be a global leader in healthy nutrition with approximately $8.5 billion in annual sales. With about 16,000 employees and 14 manufacturing sites, it will have scale across developed and emerging markets and will be well positioned to capitalize on consumer health and nutrition trends, including metabolic health, prevention and wellness.
As an independent company, it will be better positioned to focus its resources more strategically across innovation, commercial activities and key initiatives that advance performance and long-term value creation.
Its portfolio of iconic global brands with leadership positions across infant, pediatric, medical and adult nutrition is highly differentiated in its competitive set and backed by evidence-based scientific research and healthcare professional recommendation, which drives durable organic growth at scale across channels. Abbott's Nutrition portfolio is anchored by category-leading brands, including Ensure, the world's No. 1 adult nutrition supplement drink; PediaSure, the world's No. 1 pediatric nutrition supplement; Glucerna, the world's No. 1 diabetes management nutrition brand; and Similac, the No. 1 infant formula brand in the U.S.
The Nutrition business has continued to innovate its portfolio – underpinned by consumer preferences and trends – with 10 product launches in the first half of 2026, including a high-protein Ensure shake featuring 42 grams of protein, the first and only ready-to-feed liquid infant formula made with whole milk in the U.S. under the Similac brand, and dye-free Pedialyte products.
Daniel Salvadori, executive vice president and group president, Established Pharmaceuticals and Nutritional Products, will become chief executive officer of the new Nutrition company. Mr. Salvadori joined Abbott in 2014 and has successfully led complex international businesses, as senior vice president, Established Pharmaceuticals, Latin America and executive vice president of Nutritional Products before being appointed to his current position in 2021. Prior to Abbott, he held leadership roles at CFR Pharmaceuticals and Sandoz.
Abbott: A fast-growing global health leader Abbott will remain one of the largest, fastest growing and most diversified healthcare companies with unique breadth and scale. After the transaction, Abbott will have sales of approximately $42 billion and market-leading positions in cardiovascular and neuromodulation devices; biowearables; laboratory, point-of-care and cancer diagnostics; and established medicines. Abbott's portfolio helps people manage a range of conditions and enable informed and earlier clinical decision making.
The company remains aligned with evolving and durable healthcare trends, including an aging population, growing prevalence of chronic disease, personalized treatment and greater demand for earlier diagnosis so people can stay and get healthy. Abbott will maintain a balanced portfolio of products and payors with a strong presence across both developed and emerging markets.
Transaction Details Abbott intends to separate the Nutrition business through a distribution of shares of the independent Nutrition company to Abbott shareholders. Upon completion of the separation, Abbott shareholders will own shares in both Abbott and the independent Nutrition company.
Abbott expects the combined dividend to be paid by Abbott and the new Nutrition company to be equal to Abbott's dividend at the time of separation. The transaction is intended to qualify as a tax-free separation for U.S. federal income tax purposes.
Abbott expects to complete the transaction by the end of 2027, subject to customary conditions, including regulatory approvals, the effectiveness of a registration statement on Form 10 and final approval by the Abbott Board of Directors.
The planned separation will not impact Abbott's guidance for 2026 or the guidance for 2027 that Abbott plans to provide in January. Abbott expects to incur one-time charges related to the transaction during the periods preceding the separation, to be quantified at a later date.
The Nutrition business will continue to operate as part of Abbott throughout the separation process.
Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC is serving as financial advisor to Abbott, and Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz is serving as legal counsel to Abbott.

Saudi Arabia has held talks with a senior Syrian military delegation on arrangements to transfer up to 10,000 Syrian fighters to take part in the war against Yemen's Houthi movement, according to a report by the Lebanese Hezbollah-owned Al-Akhbar newspaper, citing Yemeni intelligence sources.
The report claims Syrian military officials visited Saudi Arabia's southern regions of Najran and Asir to inspect sites prepared to receive the fighters, while discussions in Riyadh covered transport logistics, financing and military assignments.
The Syrian delegation included Brig. Gen. Khaled Khattab, former commander of the Ansar al-Tawhid faction and current commander of the 82nd Division in the new Syrian army; and Brig. Gen.Haitham al-Ali, also known as Abu Muslim, commander of the army's Third Corps and a former leader in Hayat Tahrir al-Sham.
Khattab reportedly spent four days in southern Saudi Arabia, accompanied by Saudi officers, visiting sites in the regions of Asir and Najran being prepared to receive Syrian fighters. Meanwhile, al-Ali held several meetings with Saudi officers at the Defense Ministry in Riyadh to discuss the costs of transferring around 10,000 fighters, financial arrangements, additional benefits and their intended military tasks. The delegation reportedly finalized logistical arrangements for the transfer.
The report also raises the possibility that foreign fighters currently in Syria, including Uyghurs, Uzbeks, Tajiks and other nationalities, could be transferred to Yemen.
A missile industry veteran has been tapped as Iran's new defense minister, replacing the previous minister who was killed on Feb. 28, the first day of U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran.
Iranian parliamentarians overwhelmingly approved the appointment of Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi, 68, as the country's new defense chief on Sunday.
Akhlaghi studied chemical engineering at Amirkabir University of Technology and then spent more than four decades working in Iran's military industries, holding senior positions in the Shahid Bagheri Industrial Group, the Aerospace Industries Organization  – which has worked on missile development in cooperation with Russia, China and North Korea –  and the Defense Industries Organization.
He worked with Hassan Tehrani Moghaddam, a senior Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander widely regarded as the father of Iran's missile industry.
Akhlaghi has been under international sanctions since 2007 because of his involvement in Iran's missile programs.
His appointment comes as Iran works to rebuild its military facilities and replenish weapons lost during the war. He has pledged to strengthen domestic arms production, and his background suggests rebuilding Iran's missile programs will be a priority for the ministry.
Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia has claimed repeatedly since late August that Iran has rebuilt its weapons manufacturing capacity, including last week, when it said the country was now able to make more arms than " even before it [the war] began ."
Early in the war, the U.S. military said it had destroyed more than 85% of Iran's "defense industrial base," and President Trump had previously claimed Iran's military capabilities were destroyed by U.S. strikes, but experts have questioned that assessment, and Iran has demonstrated an ongoing capacity to launch attacks on ships in the region.
A Qatari aircraft arrived in Tehran Tuesday just minutes after a plane carrying Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, departed. The Qatari plane left the Iranian capital approximately 30 minutes later, according to aviation tracking data cited by Iran's semi-official Fars News agency.
The aircraft's short stay raised questions about whether it might have been carrying a diplomatic message amid ongoing indirect negotiations between the U.S. and Iran. Qatar is among the nations that have acted as mediators between the two sides for months.
No information about the aircraft's passengers or why it was in Tehran for only half an hour were provided in the Fars report.
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels said they had targeted a Saudi military operations room at Badr Camp in Aden, in southwest Yemen, with a ballistic missile on Wednesday.
Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree, in a post on X , called the strike a direct hit.
"Our armed forces successfully targeted the enemy Saudi operations room at Badr Camp in Aden with a ballistic missile. The strike was accurate and direct," he said.
Aden is the de facto seat of power of Yemen's Saudi-backed government, which was forced to decamp after the Houthis occupied the national capital Sanaa more than a decade ago.
The attack claimed by the Houthis Wednesday was the third in a week on Aden.
A police official in Aden told the French news agency AFP earlier that there had been a blast "caused by a Houthi missile." Two other security sources told AFP the strike targeted a site near the city's airport.

"The Americans and their allies have significant investments, and if they want to damage our infrastructure, it is natural that the Islamic Republic will use all its capabilities and easily destroy their investments and assets, including the internet cables that pass beneath the waters of the Strait of Hormuz," he said.
Analysts say cutting the cables in the waterway would most likely affect internet connectivity in Persian Gulf countries .
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday that Tehran and Washington were still engaged in indirect negotiations via mediators over the seven-day ceasefire proposal presented by Iran in September.
Araghchi said the U.S. was seeking to add further clauses to the Iranian proposal, which Mr. Trump rejected last month.
The proposal called for the end of the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports and vessels, the lifting of sanctions on Iranian oil sales, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the release of frozen Iranian assets.
He said Pakistan and Qatar were among the nations facilitating the indirect talks between Iran and the U.S., as they have been for months.
"The negotiating table remains in place," Araghchi said. "It is the American side that is closing the path, not Iran."

articles.title_zh: Helen Haines has lost both legs after alleged attack but ‘her heart and mind are in good shape’, husband says
articles.content_orig:
Haines is in stable condition. Surgeons tried to save her right leg but both have now been amputated due to injuries

The independent MP Helen Haines has lost both legs but remains in a stable condition, two days after an alleged targeted attack near her electorate office in north-east Victoria.
Haines, the federal MP for Indi, had been in a critical but stable condition after she was struck by a car in Wangaratta on Monday afternoon. Surgeons were trying to save her right leg on Tuesday, but both legs had to be amputated due to the seriousness of her injuries.
Her husband, Phil Haines, provided an update on his wife’s condition at Melbourne’s Alfred hospital late on Wednesday afternoon.
Composed and clear, he said his wife had survived a “horrendous incident” and faced a long road to recovery.
“The good news in all this is Helen is alive and she’s stable,” he said.
“That is the most important thing for our family. And I think when we reflect and talk about and think about Helen, the two most important parts of Helen for us as a family are her heart and her mind.
“Her heart is huge. She is a very compassionate, caring, loving person. Incredibly supportive of all around her – her family, her community, anybody she comes across. And her mind. She has the sharpest intellect.”
Phil Haines described his wife, 65, as a fighter. The pair have been married for nearly 40 years and have three children and two grandchildren. He became emotional for a moment at the end of the statement, reflecting on his wife’s strength.
“She is a determined person who will do her best with our support and love to recover, and that is what we hope for,” he said.
“We are grateful at this stage that both her heart and her mind are in good shape.”
Haines asked for donations to Save the Children as his wife recovers. A special appeal has been launched by the charity.
Police allege Monday’s attack was targeted, and have charged Brendan Nugent with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and the commonwealth offence of causing harm to a commonwealth public official.
Nugent faced Wangaratta magistrates court earlier on Wednesday.
Phil Haines was joined by the governor general, Sam Mostyn. Mostyn said she had relayed news of the incident to King Charles and praised Helen Haines’s work as a local representative, including her commitment to improving the standards of public discourse in Australia.
“This violent attack on a much loved and respected sitting member of our federal parliament must be a moment for us to pause and to choose to be better,” she said.
“We’ve got to hope that that beautiful heart, that beautiful mind will be strengthened every day by our support and our commitment to be more like Helen as part of this great democracy.”
Anthony Albanese and politicians from across federal parliament have expressed shock and anger at the alleged attack on Haines.
The incident has sparked calls for changes to politicians’ safety, with security services including the Australian federal police and Asio briefing MPs on the current landscape on Wednesday.
Speaking at a vigil in Wodonga on Wednesday evening, Cathy McGowan, who held the seat of Indi before Haines, paid tribute to her friend.
“There is another level of grief, different and deeper from the actual violence, from the sorrow, the shame and the hurt,” she said.
“It’s about Helen in her role as our elected representative. In attacking her, we intuit that this is an attack on our political system, on our democracy, and especially so for all the supporters who did the democracy work getting Helen elected.”
McGowan called for the upcoming Victorian state election campaign to be conducted in a positive and constructive way. Voters go to the polls next month.
The community could not let violence win, McGowan implored.
“That we ensure the legacy of this attack on Helen will be a stronger, more vibrant and effective democracy, and from a personal perspective, all candidates and especially women, know they can run for office and be safe.”

articles.title_orig: Elon Musk Says SpaceX and Tesla Are Exploring a Merger
articles.title_zh: Elon Musk Says SpaceX and Tesla Are Exploring a Merger
articles.content_orig:
Elon Musk on Tuesday said SpaceX and Tesla are exploring a merger — a business combination that one Wall Street analyst said could be worth nearly $5 trillion, which would make it the largest deal in corporate history.
"Both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss this idea at the request of shareholders, and these special committees consist of independent directors," Musk said during SpaceX's earnings call with investors, adding that he sees "a lot of merit to combining the companies."
Tesla's stock price rose $14.01, or 3.8%, to $387.72, while SpaceX shares jumped $14.62, or 9.9%, to $162.41 in morning trading. Here's what to know about a possible merger between the companies.
The merger would likely be valued at close to $5 trillion, Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at investment firm Yorkville Ives & Co., told CBS News.
SpaceX is currently valued at $1.98 trillion, while Tesla's market capitalization stands at about $1.5 trillion. But Tesla shareholders would likely demand a premium for their shares to agree to the merger, Ives noted.
"For the merger to get passed by shareholders, it would have to be a higher price for Tesla — likely in the $500/$550 per share range in our view," he said.
That would make the combined company one of the most valuable in the world, rivaling that of the most highly valued businesses like chipmaker Nvidia, worth $5.2 trillion, or Apple, valued at $4.95 trillion.
The main reason for combining SpaceX, a space exploration and AI company, with an electric vehicle manufacturer is to position them for a future in which artificial intelligence, or what Musk terms "super intelligence," becomes increasingly essential to everyday life.
"There's a lot to be gained from cooperating on developing super intelligence software, chip design, the Terafab obviously, robotics, mass to orbit with the Starmind constellation," Musk said in Tuesday's earnings call.
While Tesla's primary business remains manufacturing EVs, Musk has signaled that the company is shifting away from traditional motor vehicles. In January, the Tesla CEO said the company would phase out production of its Model S and Model X vehicles.
Instead, the company is changing course to focus on developing autonomous products, such as self-driving taxis and humanoid robots. Musk said Tesla will eventually produce 1 million humanoid robots a year as the company transitions to an "autonomous future." The humanoid robot, called Optimus, could hit the market in 2027, Musk said in January.
AI is essential to Optimus, allowing it to follow orders and take on various tasks, as well as to Tesla's push into self-driving robotaxis.
Meanwhile, SpaceX owns xAI, Musk's AI unit that created Grok, the chatbot that is used in the social media app X and other Musk-owned products. Musk's planned Terafab chip factory will tie all the businesses together by manufacturing semiconductors for both SpaceX and Tesla.
Combining the businesses makes sense for a "number of strategic AI and data-driven reasons, and this is the right move for Musk," Ives said in a research note.
On Tuesday's conference call, Musk underlined that a merger of SpaceX and Tesla is far from assured, noting that a majority of Tesla shareholders would need to vote in favor of the combination.
"I think some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it," he said.
Musk added, "At the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this, and particularly on the Tesla side, we will need a 50% vote of all shares, not just those who vote, but of all shareholders. And that's quite a high hurdle to try to achieve."
Even so, Ives assigns an 80% to 90% chance that the merger will happen by the end of 2027.

articles.title_orig: ‘This Is Not a Drill’: Critical PHP Vulnerabilities Are Setting the Internet on Fire
articles.title_zh: ‘This Is Not a Drill’: Critical PHP Vulnerabilities Are Setting the Internet on Fire
articles.content_orig:
Internet security and web administration teams around the world are scrambling to prevent widespread disaster. On Wednesday, the developers behind the much-used PHP programming language released emergency security updates designed to fix critical flaws that could be exploited to allow attackers to gain dangerous remote control of victim systems.
The PHP Foundation detailed the two critical vulnerabilities— CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 —which impact “all PHP installations serving web requests” going back to PHP version 5, released in July 2004. However, only PHP 8.2 and newer are still supported and will receive patches, according to the alert. The PHP Foundation noted, though, that some PHP distributions and third-party vendors still produce legacy fixes. The caveat is significant, because ubiquitous and foundational web layers like PHP can persist forgotten and un-updated in historic internet infrastructure.
“There are no complete mitigations, updating is the only safe choice,” the PHP Foundation wrote in its advisories. Security experts warn of the potential dire consequences of overlooking unpatched systems.
“This is not a drill,” says Lukasz Olejnik, an independent security consultant and visiting senior research fellow at King’s College London. Since its development in the 1990s, PHP has evolved into an essential scripting language for web development and is used across vast swaths of the internet in websites and software. Everything from publishing systems like WordPress and Drupal to e-commerce platforms like Adobe’s Magento are built on PHP.
Olejnik likens the widespread use of the programming language to critical infrastructure.
“The impact is enormous,” he says of PHP’s security flaws, adding that millions of systems could be impacted. “Especially if attackers would turn to exploiting these vulnerabilities fast. Worst case is wormable malware affecting big chunks of the internet.”
The overriding fear for security teams and developers is that malicious hackers could quickly jump upon the vulnerabilities and begin exploiting deployments before they are fixed. Internet infrastructure company Cloudflare reported it was “seeing early attacks emerging” before the PHP Foundation had detailed the vulnerabilities and released fixes. “We expect mass attacks to start within 15 minutes of the release,” security firm Sansec wrote ahead of the fixes, which were released just before 10 am ET on Wednesday.
“Most of the web runs on PHP and this bug is in a file upload interface that’s like a front door with no lock,” says longtime security and compliance consultant Davi Ottenheimer. “An attacker does not need to know which site they are hitting or even the actual software it runs. They send one crafted upload to any server they can find, and that is the entire attack.”
Ahead of the updated versions of PHP becoming available, some organizations took their websites offline as a precautionary measure. Multiple sites belonging to the Finnish government, including the National Land Survey, were inaccessible, according to reports . French government websites and the Port of Rotterdam’s website were also offline, according to Reuters .
“Everybody should patch immediately, exploitation may happen very fast and at a scale,” says Olejnik. “AI makes exploiting such vulnerabilities of immediate importance. Like, indeed, a minute or so.”
Security company Wiz, which is owned by Google, claimed its researchers discovered the vulnerabilities in PHP partially using AI tools, while OpenAI and security firm Calif also say they independently discovered the issues and worked together. Dubbing an exploitation demonstration php2shell , the Wiz researchers write that in some cases the vulnerabilities can be exploited “fairly easily.”
“The vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on affected servers or read sensitive process memory,” Wiz writes in its research. “That memory may contain passwords, authentication tokens, API keys and certificates belonging to other requests or the server itself.”
Details of the upcoming vulnerabilities first appeared from the maintainers behind PHP on October 20. In a short post on the PHP website, the PHP Foundation wrote it was giving “advance notice” of the security flaws and upcoming release of the fixes. While omitting specific details about the vulnerabilities or the versions impacted, it said both flaws are considered to have a “critical” 9.2 score out of 10 on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS).
“We reserve the right to release earlier should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild,” the security warning on the PHP site said ahead of Wednesday’s release. According to reports from Bleeping Computer and Ars Technica , some details about the vulnerabilities may have leaked before they were due to officially be published.
The early warning from the PHP Foundation may have given some developers, security teams, and companies enough of a heads up to start preparing to update systems using PHP. Ahead of the details being published, warnings from the EU’s Computer Emergency Response Team (EU-CERT) and Australia's cybersecurity agency said IT teams should be prepared to update their systems as soon as possible, with the potential for websites to be taken offline while fixes are applied.
Similarly, the UK’s National Cyber Security Center (NCSC), published an alert saying organizations should “prepare for immediate updating of systems” using PHP. “Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organizations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated,” the agency wrote online.
The NCSC advises that organizations and businesses should identify systems running PHP across their tech infrastructure. There should be a particular focus on systems using PHP that are connected to the internet, including monitoring them for any potential exploitation. The next step is applying PHP updates as they are available and monitoring for updates from software companies as they may use PHP within their apps or services.
“If you find signs of compromise, isolate the system, preserve your web server and PHP logs, and report it to your local FBI field office,” Brett Leatherman, the FBI’s cyber assistant director posted online. “Those reports help us identify the actors involved and warn other organizations before they become victims.”

articles.title_orig: Anthropic to publicly file for IPO as early as Friday, sources say
articles.title_zh: Anthropic to publicly file for IPO as early as Friday, sources say
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) is set to publicly file its S-1 investor prospectus as soon as Friday, according to three people familiar with the artificial intelligence firm's plans. The move would mark a crucial next step for what could be the biggest IPO in history.
The much-anticipated public debut , expected to surpass SpaceX's ( SPCX ) June IPO, is widely viewed as a crucial test of investor appetite for the artificial intelligence boom, as investors have become more concerned about the industry's massive spending.
Anthropic confidentially submitted a draft IPO registration statement to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in June. Under SEC rules, companies using the confidential process must make their registration materials available 15 calendar days before the start of their formal investor roadshow.
Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment on the timing of its S-1.
A public filing would clear a key procedural hurdle toward a potential November listing, though the timing of the offering remains subject to market conditions and other factors. Crucially, it would also give regular investors their first look at the financial details and risks around one of the AI industry's fastest-growing companies.
Anthropic is spending billions on AI infrastructure to train and run its suite of Claude models. That includes working with Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) and Amazon ( AMZN ), as well as renting out graphics processor unit (GPU) capacity from SpaceX's Colossus 1 data center.
The company pulled in $16.3 billion in revenue over the first six months of 2026 and reported a net loss of over $80 billion, according to a Tuesday Wall Street Journal report . Wall Street is anticipating that the company could raise as much as $100 billion at a $2 trillion valuation, Reuters previously reported .
Last week, Anthropic told investors at its San Francisco office that its revenue climbed to $16.8 billion in the third quarter, up from $11.5 billion in the second quarter, according to the Financial Times , noting that the company is also profitable on an adjusted basis.
The colossal offering comes as this year's banner IPO market is becoming more challenging. Earlier this week, shares of South Korean data center provider Elice plummeted a staggering 32% during its first trading day after raising $151 million. Nvidia-backed Firmus Grid abruptly shelved plans for a public listing earlier this month after investors balked at its proposed valuation, while several other companies have postponed plans to go public, citing market conditions.
Publicly traded AI-related companies have also waffled in recent days as investors become more selective over the industry's enormous spending needs. CoreWeave, in particular, has come under sharp scrutiny as investors question its future revenue prospects relative to its debt load.
The shift highlights how investors who enthusiastically bid up AI-related companies earlier this year have become more selective.
Given its enormous size, the timing of Anthropic's IPO is also expected to be a significant factor for other companies seeking to go public in the coming weeks, one person said.
CEO Dario Amodei co-founded Anthropic with his sister Daniela, the company's president.
Anthropic established a strong foothold in the enterprise market with its Claude chatbot, the popular AI coding tool Claude Code, and Claude Cowork.
Rival OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ), which was initially expected to launch its IPO this year, is now projected to hit the public markets in early 2027.

articles.title_orig: UK government approves a natural gas project off Scotland despite environmental concerns
articles.title_zh: UK government approves a natural gas project off Scotland despite environmental concerns
articles.content_orig:
Lord Frost led the negotiations that finally took Britain out of the EU in 2020.  A Cabinet minister in the Boris Johnson government, he resigned in protest at the handling of Covid lockdowns, and has since been a persistent advocate of a more fully conservative approach to policy on the Right. He is a non-affiliated peer in the House of Lords.
Even a stopped clock is right twice a day. And every so often even this Labour government gets something right. The approval of the Jackdaw North Sea gas field is one such moment. Of course, it is to be welcomed. But enabling Britain to use its own gas really ought to be the ordinary business of government, not an occasion for national rejoicing.
After all, it has taken 20 years to get to this point. Jackdaw was discovered in 2005 . Rishi Sunak’s government licensed it, only to be blocked by the courts. Now finally we have definitive approval. Gas will flow before the end of the year. At last.
Jackdaw is not a panacea. The Government expects it to increase domestic gas production by around 6 per cent at its peak, with a lifespan of up to 11 years. That is about 2 per cent of UK demand. There may not be a huge impact on prices, but that is not the point. The case for Jackdaw is that we should use our own oil and gas, not other people’s.
Domestic production supports jobs, tax revenues and security of supply. It has downstream effects on the wider British economy that buying Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) from Qatar or the US, still less wind turbines or solar panels from China, simply do not have. The green case against all this amounts to saying that producing things in Britain is pointless unless doing so helps determine the world price. Follow that logic and Britain wouldn’t make anything much – a nation of spectators, buying in everything and producing nothing.
It is true, of course, that Jackdaw only supports a couple of dozen jobs directly. But once again that is the point. Producing a lot of something we want with only a few jobs and no government subsidy is a good thing. We get lots of gas, and everyone else can go and do something else that also adds to the national wealth. That increase in productivity is why we aren’t all still tilling the fields. Jobs are a cost, not a benefit. The much-vaunted tens of thousands of “green jobs” in the heavily subsidised “net zero economy” represent a move from a productive to a less productive energy system. They are therefore not part of the solution but part of the problem.
That’s why what matters is not so much the Jackdaw decision, which was a no-brainer in current circumstances, but whether that decision represents a new trajectory. On that, one must be unconvinced. Yes, it’s obvious that the Starmer government and Ed Miliband, in particular, did not want to license Jackdaw .
Andy Burnham’s Government, more in touch with the unions, not just Labour “progressives”, read the room better. But what happens next? After all, they could have approved Rosebank too. They didn’t. If it’s approved in future, they will get another day of criticism from the cranky green Left that they could have avoided. So one must be suspicious. One look at the stony faces on the benches behind Burnham told you everything about Labour’s real level of enthusiasm.
The real charge against ministers on the back of the decision is not that they have abandoned their policy. It is that they have not. Even now, the Government is announcing a new “Energy Wealth Fund” designed to channel North Sea tax revenues into renewable and low-carbon projects. That’s one signal that there will be no letting up on the subsidised move to renewables.
And here’s another. Burnham described the Jackdaw decision as a “bridge to the future”. Unite’s Sharon Graham is giving the Government a bit of cover for this, presenting it as buying time to support investment in industries like “wind turbine manufacture and refining green jet fuel”. Call me sceptical about whether we can build a windmill industry at Chinese expense. And green jet fuel is a fantasy project if ever there were one, especially with the lights going out across Britain’s refining industry one plant at a time.
The Government is simply not facing up to the scale of the energy problem we face. British industrial energy prices are roughly four times those in the US. Microsoft has withdrawn from Nscale’s Loughton data centre project after its expected electricity grid connection slipped into the 2030s. OpenAI paused the UK element of the massive Stargate project in April, citing energy costs and regulation. We aren’t going to maintain our (just about) prominent position on AI when the electricity is unavailable or unaffordable.
The grid itself is increasingly rickety. On June 23, frequency fell below normal operating limits for a prolonged period. No one really knows how close we came to a shutdown. This week’s report from Eversheds Sutherland does not shed much light on the subject, but does make clear that there were serious concerns among staff at the energy grid operator about the situation. On far too many days this autumn we have had to rely on buying electricity at super-inflated prices through the European interconnectors, and it hasn’t even started to get cold yet. cold yet.
The Jackdaw decision helps. But it isn’t a change of the net zero policy: indeed the Government is going out of its way to tell us it isn’t. That’s the real problem.
It has to be understood that the more renewables we build, the more our electricity depends on the weather, the more expensive back-up is, and thus the more problems we have. We know the Government doesn’t get this, but even Kemi Badenoch said in Parliament on Wednesday that “of course we need renewables”. We don’t. We need oil, gas, and nuclear. Refusal to face this is not buying our country global influence. No-one outside the hold-outs in parts of the EU cares. Reordering the economy around a carbon target is not responsible stewardship if the price is industrial decline and poorer households.
The energy clock has not stopped. It is ticking, and ticking down to economic decline, unless the policy changes. An energy strategy that simply makes Britain poorer and colder is not in the interests of the British people. It is a failure of government dressed up as a moral achievement.

articles.title_orig: Israeli Military Detains Brad Lander in West Bank During Volunteer Trip
articles.title_zh: Israeli Military Detains Brad Lander in West Bank During Volunteer Trip
articles.content_orig:
• A new low: President Donald Trump’s approval rating stands at a record low of 32%, a CNN poll shows . Democrats enter the midterms with a 10-point advantage over Republicans nationwide.
• Candidate detained and released: Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander has been released after being detained today by the Israeli military. He had been accompanying Palestinian olive pickers and activists in the occupied West Bank.
• Another red-state rally : Trump will travel to South Carolina today to campaign for Sen. Darline Graham , who is seeking a full term after being appointed to her late brother Sen. Lindsey Graham’s seat. She is in a tough contest against Democratic candidate Annie Andrews despite Trump winning the state two years ago by 18 points.
• Ohio governor’s race: Republican nominee Vivek Ramaswamy’s campaign is drawing fierce pushback over a viral campaign video of his Democratic opponent’s estranged mother telling voters to reject her. Vice President JD Vance will be in Ohio today to campaign for Ramaswamy, a source said.
Illinois first lady MK Pritzker, the wife of Gov. JB Pritzker, announced today she was donating $500,000 to support Ohio Democrats and Amy Acton, the party’s gubernatorial nominee in the Buckeye State.
Pritzker in a statement referenced the ad campaign produced by Acton’s opponent, Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, that featured Acton’s estranged mother and drew criticism from even some Republicans .
Individual campaign contribution limits in Ohio are capped at $16,615.67 per election for statewide candidates. A spokesperson for Pritzker said she donated that amount to Acton’s campaign, and the remainder to the Ohio Democratic Party.
“Darline is not Lindsey” is a phrase often repeated around South Carolina these days.
Even after a crash course in politics this summer following her brother’s sudden death, Darline Graham, the candidate, remains very different from Lindsey Graham, the candidate. Her campaign performance is coming under increased scrutiny as Republicans in South Carolina and Washington rush to bolster her with millions in new ad spending.
Democratic nominee Annie Andrews is newly competitive in a state President Donald Trump won two years ago by 18 points. A Democrat hasn’t won a Senate seat in South Carolina since 1998.
Subscribers can read more here.
New York Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander says he was released from Israeli military custody “with a ‘warning’” after he was detained today while accompanying Palestinian olive pickers and activists in the occupied West Bank.
Video shared by activist groups shows the former New York comptroller being loaded onto a bus by an Israeli police officer.
An ally of New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Lander won the Democratic primary for a US House seat earlier this year and is expected to win in the midterm election in two weeks.
Lander, who is Jewish, posted a photo of himself detained on a bus with other volunteers on X , writing: “The occupation is a crime under international law. Harvesting olives isn’t a crime under any law I know.”
Dozens of volunteers and activists remain detained, with Lander calling for their immediate release.
Well-known Israeli activist Andrey X, who regularly provides protective presence to Palestinians in the West Bank, was also detained, according to footage shared with CNN by his colleague, Jasper Nathaniel.
Some 90 volunteers from the Israeli organization Rabbis for Human Rights were accompanying Palestinian farmers, alongside Lander, to land they haven’t been able to reach in three years when they were detained in the village of Nahalin near Bethlehem, according to a statement from the group.
In a statement, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said the olive harvest near the Israeli settlement of Beitar Illit was “uncoordinated,” saying harvesting in the area requires a request at the beginning of the season.
Some context: The olive harvest season in the West Bank has become synonymous with settler violence, often backed by Israeli forces. This year especially has seen daily attacks on farmers and communities who rely on harvesting for their livelihoods.
This post has been updated with Lander’s release and additional details.
President Donald Trump’s approval rating stands at a record low of 32%, according to a new CNN poll conducted by SSRS, and voters express broad dissatisfaction with both the economy and the state of the country nearly two years into unified GOP control of the federal government.
Trump’s approval rating is a new low by one point, and 7 points lower than his approval rating just before the 2018 midterms.
The share who strongly approve of his presidency stands at just 13%, down 17 points from Trump’s last midterms.
Americans are judging Trump’s performance against a political landscape that looks very different than it did eight years ago. In the autumn of 2018, a 55% majority of the public said things in the US were generally going well, and 69% called economic conditions good. Weeks before the 2026 midterms, those numbers stand at 30% and 26%, respectively.
And while in 2018, the economy was a bright spot for Trump – most approved of his handling of the issue, even while his ratings stood underwater overall – it’s now the factor most weighing him down.
Trump’s approval ratings on economic issues are lower than his rating overall, with 27% approving on the economy and just 23% on inflation.
Two-thirds of Americans, including roughly one-third of Republicans, say that his policies have made economic conditions worse. And even as majorities say that Trump has gone too far in using his presidential power and overseeing deportations, nearly 7 in 10 say he has not gone far enough in trying to reduce prices.
Read more of the poll’s findings.
President Donald Trump has often complained that the Democratic Party is obsessed with “Russia, Russia, Russia.”
But it’s the president who dragged his deferential relationship with President Vladimir Putin into the current midterm election campaign, with his sanctions-busting diesel deal with Moscow and by lashing out at Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
Still, there was some good news on Wednesday with the release of Stephen Hubbard , a 74-year-old American jailed in Russia for more than four years on charges of fighting for Ukraine, who has been in poor health.
But Trump envoy Steve Witkoff’s latest shower of praise for Putin is likely to cause more pain in Ukraine and incite more pre-election criticism of the president’s Russia policy ahead of the midterms.
The word “humanitarian” rarely springs to mind to describe Putin, who launched an unprovoked assault on Ukraine that has killed tens of thousands and has been accused of war crimes by the International Criminal Court.
And while flattery is part of diplomacy, Witkoff’s pattern of repeatedly lionizing Putin will only fuel concerns in Ukraine and among its allies that the Trump administration is hardly an honest broker in the war.
Everyone will be happy that Hubbard is free. But GOP candidates can expect more tough questions over Trump and Russia on the trail.
President Donald Trump’s political operation entered the final weeks of the midterm campaign with nearly $181 million in cash reserves to help boost his party’s House and Senate candidates, new filings show.
Trump’s team already has spent staggering sums on the election — $300 million by his own account — and the balance sheets of the political committees aligned with Trump show he has ample resources to fulfill his pledge to spend $400 million by Election Day.
His main super PAC, MAGA Inc., has brought in more than $464 million, an unprecedented sum for a term-limited president. Donations to it from wealthy individuals and corporations have helped fuel advertising and voter outreach across multiple competitive contests this fall as the president works to salvage the GOP’s majority in Congress.

articles.content_orig:
Nintendo is welcoming the spooky season the only way it knows how: with a big old eShop sale, of course!
The ' Screaming Deals ' sale is now live on the North American eShop, bringing welcome discounts to a whole host of Switch 1 and 2 bangers until 31st October at 11:59 PT — so make sure you've made the most of it by then!
There are so many games on sale, in fact, that we have assembled the following list to showcase the cream of the crop, pulling every 'Screaming Deals' game we rated a 9/10 or higher (plus one personal pick from those that fell below the review bar, because we couldn't resist).

Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.
Ace Combat 7: Skies Unknown is the absolute pinnacle of the series and despite coming to Switch over five years after other platforms, this 'impossible' Switch conversion does very little to degrade the experience. Long-time franchise players and military aviation enthusiasts will be overwhelmed by the fan service at every turn, from craters on the ground to airplanes, liveries, callsigns, and emblems shouting out to previous entries.
We understand the genre is uniquely niche, but if this is your first foray into the franchise, this conversion is a perfect gateway into this rich, revered series. You get tons of content and an epic single-player campaign wrapped up in triple-A presentation that delivers the most comprehensive portable experience ever from Project Aces.
Alien: Isolation is a survival horror masterpiece and straight-up one of the very best horror video games ever released.
It's a nerve-wracking affair — a slow, methodical game of cat and mouse against a brilliantly clever recreation of one of cinema's most infamous killers — but if you're up to the task you'll find one of the most satisfying gameplay experiences in the genre; a brilliant and beautiful homage to one of the greatest sci-fi movies of all time.
Feral Interactive has done a stellar job with this Switch port and the excellent motion controls and inclusion of all previously-released DLC only go to sweeten the deal. This is essential stuff for survival horror fans.
Developer Shared Memory's stated goal was “to craft complete experiences that will be playable long after the world loses its internet connection,” and screen after screen, Animal Well excels in delighting your eyes and giving your brain something to stew on.
It’s a riposte against a culture of post-launch updates in favour of a meticulously crafted, singular vision with potentially years’ worth of discoveries baked in. By all indications, Animal Well delivers on that long-term promise and does so with a one-of-a-kind elegance.
A slice of Viking strategic combat right out of the heart of Scandinavia’s indie development scene, Bad North was at the vanguard of a wave of smart yet intrinsically accessible real-time strategy titles.
Swedish developer Plausible Concept calls it ‘micro-strategy’ and it's the perfect encapsulation of a minimalist approach that covers everything from unit management to the Monument Valley -style isometric art style.
With enough enemy variance to convince you you’re playing an interactive episode of the Vikings TV show, this endlessly entertaining sea of bitesize battles will teach you to fear — and love — the sound of the oncoming horde.
Balatro is a roguelike for gamers who don't like roguelikes... and then everybody else on top of that. It utterly nails what it sets out to do, providing an instantly accessible, satisfying, and addictive gameplay loop that anybody can grasp.
It's an immensely enjoyable experience from the start, but as you get deeper in, there's really nothing else quite like it. Sublime.
It looks like The Witness and it plays a bit like StreetPass Garden , but Botany Manor blooms into something that's not only entirely its own, but also something quite special. Don't let its cosy aesthetics fool you — Botany Manor is packed with nicely challenging, well-designed puzzles, and isn't afraid to tackle heavy subjects, too.
As an adventure game, Chicory: A Colorful Tale is quite sincerely up there with the very best of the genre.
There’s plenty to see and do and a full completion run will probably take you 25-30 hours. The characters and their travails are rich and likeable, the game’s sense of humour is generally inspired, and it’s all very sweet without being sugary-twee and talking down to the player. It’s also an affecting little tearjerker that will definitely strike a chord if you make art, and almost certainly will even if you don’t – so long as you’re capable of pretty basic empathy.
Chicory is simple to play but impressively long and complex, with perfect controls, performance and visuals. Throw yourself into painting the world and you’ll be left with a game that’s very much your own and speaks to you directly – a beautiful marriage of mechanics, themes and visuals.
While it’s a shame that there are fewer games here than in other Konami collections — we’d have loved to have seen NES title Contra Force or the now-extinct WiiWare title Contra ReBirth — the ones included in the Contra Anniversary Collection are universally brilliant. The 8-bit and 16-bit Contra games are among the finest examples of the run ‘n gun genre, and to have almost all of them included in a single release and emulated flawlessly is an absolute treat.
Whether you’re a fan of the series or a curious onlooker who’s always wanted to see what the fuss was all about, this is essential.
We really like Crawl , and we’d bet our collected stash of gold and wrath you will, too. A dungeon-crawling hack-and-slash affair with roguelike elements, one player is the hero trying to get through a dungeon and the others play as monster-controlling ghosts attempting to kill said hero and take their place.
It's an everyone-for-themselves free-for-all, yet there are opportunities for frantic 3v1 co-operative play — a necessity when all the non-hero ghost characters must take joint control of bosses the hero faces. It’s great fun in single-player thanks to some aggressive AI, but that consistent danger takes on a new dimension when you and three of your friends are jostling for XP and that all-important killing blow.
Competitive couchplay doesn’t get much better than this on Switch.
In 2023, a year dominated by titanic, big-budget releases like Tears of the Kingdom and Mario Wonder , off-the-wall roguelike Dave The Diver stepped up to the plate and knocked the ball clear of the park with a heaving swing.
Its charming animations and writing supplement a mechanically dense experience that never stops dangling a new carrot to chase. You owe it to yourself to pick up this outstandingly funny, enthralling, and weird gem.
Death's Door is a modern classic, utilising old gameplay ideas in a new setting to make for a short and sweet experience you won’t want to miss. The snappy combat, rewarding exploration, and relaxing music will stick with you once you've finished, and while it may not have anything 'new' to offer, Death’s Door is so high quality that you’ll hardly have time to think about its lack of innovation.
Any fans of Zelda or Soulslike games will adore this - Acid Nerve has crafted an experience that’s absolutely worth your time and money.
An attractive art style, strong combat system, and meaningful player choices make Dicefolk a brilliant addition to the library, as it manages to feel fresh without getting too far away from the core ideas that make these sorts of games so addictive and popular.
Dicefolk is a good entry point to the genre, in fact; approachable without being patronising and it’s tons of fun once you get a grasp of it

articles.content_orig:
The Pokémon Company has announced that a permanent Pokémon retail store is coming to London.
The store, which is due to open “by 2029,” is “the first of several permanent Pokémon stores that are planned to launch outside of Asia,” according to The Pokémon Company .
A Pokémon retail location did exist outside of Asia between 2001 and 2005, when Pokémon Center New York was open. The store then became the Nintendo Store, which it remains to this day.
Notably, The Pokémon Company isn’t calling the store a Pokémon Center, the branding used for permanent Pokémon retail stores in Japan and pop-up stores at Pokémon events.
The exact location of the store has yet to be announced.
Pokémon retail locations typically feature exclusive merchandise, in addition to merchandise that’s available on the Pokémon Center website. As the UK is one of the few regions with a dedicated Pokémon Center retail website and fufillment center, it makes sense as the first location to recieve the permanent retail store.
Chief product and experience officer at The Pokémon Company International, Gaku Susai, commented: “We are always exploring new opportunities that help us create unique and memorable experiences for our fans. This new London store will give visitors the chance to step into the world of Pokémon, whether they’re discovering the brand for the first time or have been Trainers for years.
“We hope it becomes a place where everyone can come together, feel like part of a community and enjoy the magic of Pokémon in a whole new way.”
London has become a hub of Pokémon events in recent years. The Pokémon European International Championships have taken place at London’s Excel Center for several years. These events also feature a pop-up Pokémon Center, free slots for which regularly sell out weeks ahead of time.

articles.title_orig: Why Palestinians Hope Israelis Will Oust Netanyahu in Pivotal Election
articles.title_zh: Why Palestinians Hope Israelis Will Oust Netanyahu in Pivotal Election
articles.content_orig:
Only a clear opposition victory would let us begin to heal, strengthen democracy and establish Palestinian rights
Dahlia Scheindlin is a Tel Aviv-based political analyst
I srael’s 27 October election is fast approaching, with little clarity about who will win. But Benjamin Netanyahu is more likely to lose . His polling is poor , and the fractious opposition parties may yet find a way to form the next government.
What would such a government do? Most of the Zionist opposition parties, the frontrunners to lead such a coalition, have offered bromides about good governance and unifying the country. Others have focused on more specific plans to establish a state commission of inquiry into the government’s failures around the attacks of 7 October 2023, and end the exemption from military service enjoyed by most ultra-Orthodox Jewish men.
But if a new government truly plans to build a better future, Israel needs more profound changes. Simply ousting Netanyahu will not be enough.
The two issues the opposition has highlighted are understandably important to Israelis. For so many citizens, the disaster of 7 October and subsequent two-year hostage crisis became a crisis of faith in the state itself. Without accountability through an independent inquiry, society cannot move on. And even staunch supporters of peace cannot tolerate the rank injustice of some citizens serving and dying in wars while others are systematically let off the hook.
But what then? Israel’s war in response to 7 October has continued to devastate Palestinian society. But the past few years have damaged Israel internally as well.
Social solidarity in Israel is abysmal . Hundreds of thousands of reservists have served for months, interrupting their studies, family life and income. Up to 30,000 people have been wounded, according to Israel’s ministry of defence .
Meanwhile, the current government has slashed social-service budgets in favour of defence spending. The psychological toll is immense, yet Israel had a shortage of psychiatrists even prior to the war . Dr Graciela Cors, a youth and child psychiatrist, told me: “The mental health situation is catastrophic, and so are the social systems that are supposed to support mental health, like outpatient clinics and Kupot Holim [Israel’s state-mandated health funds].”
These problems are urgent, but addressing them would amount to damage limitation. Without deeper change, better-funded services and greater conscription would do little more than help Israel cope with the next round of seemingly endless wars.
Israel desperately needs to confront the factors that brought the country to this point to begin with.
Before Hamas’s attack, 2023 was already the year these long-festering problems burst into full view. Society was torn apart by two unreconciled, deeply interconnected questions: what kind of democracy Israel should be, and what is the future for the Palestinians?
Historically, Israel has demonstrated a flawed, ambiguous commitment to democracy . It avoided writing a constitution, and has no law that explicitly guarantees equality to all citizens. But over roughly the past 15 years, that ambiguity has given way to a full-blown assault on democratic institutions. Attacks on the judiciary came from top governing officials , culminating in Netanyahu’s government’s plans in 2023 to drastically weaken judicial independence .
That top-down assault fell on fertile ground because of a deeper problem: the erosion of democratic values, shaped in part by education. Or Kashti, the former longtime education correspondent for Haaretz (where I also write), told me that the seeds of the judicial assault are found in the new civics textbook adopted in 2016 . He has traced a shift from vague treatment of democracy in earlier decades, to what he describes as “indoctrination”, with greater emphasis on Jewish identity and state power . This is a thin and misguided view of democracy, one that risks elevating the will of the majority above all other democratic values.
The curriculum can also be alarmingly parochial. Kashti says that history matriculation exams focus on the second world war and the Holocaust, the wars of modern Israeli history and the establishment of the Zionist movement. “All other topics in history of the world are marginal,” he says. Religion, he adds, infiltrates unrelated subjects. “In geography or weather lessons, children are told to learn the prayer for rain. What’s the connection between prayer for rain and a lesson on geography and climate change?”
This narrow conception of democracy helps explain how, in 2022, half the country elected parties that sought to hobble judicial institutions as part of the coalition government’s programme. And when education gives barely any attention to human rights, civil liberties and the equality of all citizens – it becomes easy to see why Palestinian self-determination has dropped off the Israeli agenda entirely.
after newsletter promotion
For decades, Israeli society has increasingly acted on the assumption that Palestinians could be contained through military force or control. In the years before 7 October, most Israelis saw no contradiction between democracy at home and their active military occupation regime effectively ruling over all Palestinians, without giving them rights or representation.
Netanyahu’s current government has pursued the logical end of occupation – permanent annexation , ever-expanding settlements and ethnic cleansing. To do that, the government had to destroy the final guardrails on its power. The 2023 assault on the judiciary finally galvanised many Israelis, who feared that their own liberties were under threat. Massive protests followed, plunging the country into prolonged social turmoil.
No Israeli government can offer a different future without fundamental and comprehensive change on these deepest issues. What is needed is a fundamental reassessment of the country’s entire social ethos.
The good news is that such change is absolutely possible. Education curriculums can be rewritten to embrace the principles of a modern liberal democracy. Teachers, politicians and even religious leaders can embrace human and civil liberties, minority rights, checks and balances, good governance and the universal values that too many Israelis disdain today. Societies and people can change.
In such a society, it would be the occupation, rather than democracy, that would become an unsustainable affront to the values of Israel. This is a long way off; the current opposition leaders demonstrate no vision leading to such an outcome, and change is needed much more urgently. Israel’s right wing and many ordinary citizens, shaped by years of fear, would fight any change favouring Palestinian independence. But without embarking on the path, the country will never get there; needless to say, Palestinians will never be free.
None of this will transpire if Netanyahu wins or if Israel’s elections yield a stalemate. But an opposition victory should be the day when the hardest, yet most hopeful, work will begin.
Dahlia Scheindlin is a Tel Aviv-based political analyst and author of The Crooked Timber of Democracy in Israel

articles.title_zh: Nvidia’s latest GPU driver brings a new way to speed up PC games
articles.content_orig:
Microsoft’s new Advanced Shader Delivery technology is now part of Nvidia’s drivers.
Microsoft’s new Advanced Shader Delivery technology is now part of Nvidia’s drivers.
Nvidia is rolling out a new GPU driver today (621.01) that enables Microsoft’s new Advanced Shader Delivery technology to speed up game launches. The technology also removes mid-game “just-in-time” shader compilation, reducing stuttering and CPU spikes.
Microsoft’s Advanced Shader Delivery works by offloading shader compilation for different hardware combinations to the cloud. “Using DirectX 12, Windows 11, and the Microsoft Agility SDK, developers capture shaders into a State Object Database (SODB), allowing Microsoft’s cloud network to precompile shaders for hundreds of thousands of hardware and driver combinations,” explains Nvidia’s Andrew Burnes .
Gears of War: E-Day and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 now both support Advanced Shader Delivery, as long as you download the games via the Xbox PC app. “This system is storefront-agnostic, meaning you benefit even when playing games purchased on Steam, as long as the Xbox PC app is installed on your PC,” says Burnes.
Advanced Shader Delivery will let you skip the annoying shader compilation screen in Call of Duty , and it should improve the overall performance of supported games. “With a near-100 percent cache hit rate, it eliminates mid-game ‘just-in-time’ shader compilation, wiping out CPU spikes and frame stutters in titles like Gears of War: E-Day , and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 .
You can download Nvidia’s latest 621.01 update here , and Advanced Shader Delivery is also supported on AMD GPUs with Adrenalin 26.6.1 or higher and Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X2 series with driver version 2026.08.3 or higher .

articles.title_orig: After A Year Of Layoffs, Disney Finds $180 Million For Recruits From Bankrupt Character.AI
articles.title_zh: After A Year Of Layoffs, Disney Finds $180 Million For Recruits From Bankrupt Character.AI
articles.content_orig:
Sign up to get our news digest — delivered directly to your inbox twice a week.
Disney has spent much of 2026 cutting jobs and announcing restrictions on employee benefits, with the reductions continuing under new CEO Josh D’Amaro. Now, it plans to spend roughly $180 million over three years to compensate and retain 66 recruits from the recently bankrupt, highly controversial chatbot startup Character.AI.
According to Business Insider , citing bankruptcy filings, the hiring follows September layoffs that included technology workers. The recruits are following former Character.AI CEO Karandeep Anand, whom Disney recently appointed its first company-wide chief technology officer. The group crossing over constitutes most of Character.AI’s approximately 86-person workforce at September’s end.
As we reported last week , Character.AI filed for Chapter 11 protection on October 12, ten days after Anand officially joined Disney. Disney separately offered $20 million for a non-exclusive, perpetual license to certain intellectual property and certain company claims, subject to the bankruptcy sale process.
The spending adds another revealing chapter to Disney’s year of restructuring and continued efforts to get ahead in the AI race. The company eliminated jobs in January, approximately 1,000 more in April, and hundreds in July, including roughly 150 at Pixar .
In September, Disney’s top lawyer warned employees that his department would shrink substantially as the company considered automation, outside providers, and outsourcing. Beginning in 2027, Disney will also restrict spousal health coverage when spouses can obtain insurance through their own employers, even if those plans offer worse benefits.
These decisions come alongside substantial profits and shareholder payouts. Disney reported $5.6 billion in fiscal third-quarter segment operating income, up 21%, and raised its fiscal-year share-buyback target to at least $9 billion.
Big picture, the layoffs, benefit restrictions, buybacks, and AI hiring reveal consistent spending priorities. Disney is willing to commit substantial sums to AI expertise (remember its proposed $1 billion investment in OpenAI, announced alongside a Sora licensing deal that collapsed just over three months later, before any money changed hands?) and shareholder returns, while asking its existing workforce to absorb repeated cuts.

Xbox vice president Jason Ronald has confirmed that game developers on Xbox will get access to FSR 4.1 support "very soon", following up on AMD's announcement of its latest-gen FSR coming to five new platforms yesterday.
It's an important development for the Xbox platform, given that Sony has already released two versions of its PSSR machine learning upscaler for PS5 Pro and recently backported a lightweight version called QSSR to the base PS5 . Now, Microsoft's ML hardware on the Xbox Series X and Series S might finally come in useful - despite launching with the consoles in 2020, we've not seen it used for upscaling thus far.
It's not clear exactly how Microsoft's FSR 4.1 implementation will work, but the language here suggests that it will be down to game developers to integrate the upscaling technology in their games, rather than Microsoft being able to provide a system-level override that automatically upgrades older FSR versions to FSR 4.1.
Either way, FSR 4.1 is capable of producing better results than the older FSR 3 model, and it'll be fascinating to see how it compares to the likes of FSR, Epic's TSR, and Sony's QSSR and PSSR in shipping games.
Microsoft has also worked with Asus and AMD to add FSR 4.1 support to Xbox Ally and Xbox Ally X handhelds, which is now available. I'm working on a review of the Intel-powered Acer Predator Atlas 8 handheld right now, and it'll be interesting to compare how the Xbox Ally X with FSR 4.1 and Atlas 8 with XeSS 3 compare in terms of image quality and performance.

Boeing's largest 737 MAX aircraft has received Federal Aviation Administration certification, clearing the way for deliveries of a jet with 1,555 orders that represent a third of the company's outstanding 737 MAX order book.
The FAA announced Tuesday that it had certified the 737 MAX 10 after years of regulatory and safety reviews, removing a major hurdle for Boeing as it prepares to begin deliveries to airlines in the coming months.
Boeing said the aircraft has received orders from more than 30 customers worldwide, making the MAX 10 a key part of the company's commercial airplane backlog.
The approval also marks a significant milestone for Boeing's 737 MAX program, which has received 7,350 orders across the aircraft family, with nearly 2,500 planes delivered through the end of September 2026.

Certification followed an extensive FAA safety review and testing program. Boeing said the process involved nearly 1,000 test flights, more than 2,000 flight hours and 1,000 hours of ground testing.

"This is a major win for American manufacturing and our nation's status as a global aviation powerhouse," Duffy said in the FAA's announcement.
