articles.title_zh: Final Fantasy Resonance Nintendo Switch 1 vs. 2 differences detailed
articles.content_orig:
From Cloud to Zidane, get a deeper insight into the RPG’s gameplay transforming cameos.
With its cinematic HD-2D visuals and flashy combat, Final Fantasy Resonance was already piquing the interest of turn-based RPG fans, but its powerful and fun Visions mechanic has really captured the imagination. I went hands-on with the final game to take a deep dive into what Visions are, how they work, and how they transform main characters Rain and Lasswell’s quest to save their world.
If you’re familiar with summons in turn-based RPGs, then that’s a good starting point for Visions – but you’ll get a particular kick out of them if you’re a long-time Final Fantasy fan. As I explored Lapis, I encountered crystal shrines that each welcomed me to engage with a short tale of a hero from previous games in the series.
After an introduction with video clips and multiple choice questions relating to the chosen Vision, I was gifted with a combat-ready assist companion that could be equipped to one of Final Fantasy Resonance’s main party members, granting different magic and attacks in combat, but also permanently enhancing baseline stats like health and speed.
All of which I’ll delve into a bit later, because let’s get into the most pertinent question first…
With so many legendary Final Fantasy heroes spanning 16 main numbered titles, series veterans will be pleased to know that a staggering 26 companions are available to find across the entire game.
These range from iconic villain Sephiroth (Final Fantasy VII) and amnesiac rebel Terra (FFVI), to the first Warrior of Light (Final Fantasy) and stoic battler Lightning (FFXIII). There’s also a handful of original characters from the game Final Fantasy Resonance has adapted and enhanced here, Final Fantasy Brave Exvius, such as Black Mage Tronn.
While most don’t typically talk outside of combat chatter, each legacy Vision feels and looks exactly how you’d want them to, complete with animations and music appropriate to the titles they’re originally known for. And yes, their attacks are just as faithful as well.
When a Vision is first awakened I immediately gained access to a basic suite of passive perks, as well as magic and physical strikes to unleash in battle. Take Noctis (FFXV), for example. His opening passive benefits are a 20% boost to my character’s attacks, and the ability to cast Thunder or Blizzard in combat.
However, as each equipped Vision earns mastery points from winning battles, more bonuses and Vision specific abilities are unlocked. In Noctis’ case, his early mastery bonuses include a 40% increase of the equipped party member’s limit burst gauge – the special meter that fills over the course of a fight and lets you deliver a powerful single attack – each time you defeat an enemy.
Unlocking further mastery levels for someone like Zidane (FFIX) means gaining access to his Steal skill, which can be boosted further with his Mug ability which adds potential damage to his theft attempt.
But by far the most spectacular use of a Vision’s power is their Resonance capability. By staggering all opponents during combat – finding their weakness and depleting their stagger meter – I was given the choice of using any of my equipped Visions’ dazzling cinematic finishers, such as Cloud’s (Final Fantasy VII) brutal Ascension Resonance.
Let’s not get it twisted – Visions may initially look like regular summon attacks, but there’s far more to them than just that. In fact, Final Fantasy Resonance has more traditional summons in the shape of Espers who can join your battles for a set number of turns.
No, Visions fundamentally alter and personalize your party’s proficiencies in combat. The more a party member uses a Vision, the greater their level of affinity grows, which in turn means more bonuses for that character. And because each Vision has a specific role/job status where they excel, I quickly learned to mix and match them to my party characters to either create specialists or all-rounders.
For example, Lasswell has the role of a Breaker, a class geared towards staggering enemies in combat. But coupling him with original Vision Medic Leah gave him the ability to use healing magic and an option to pass his combat turn to an ally, which made him my durable back-up support character if my main heavy hitter went down in battle. Allying him with Cloud (also a Breaker) later on gave my version of Lasswell even stronger offensive capabilities to keep him in the fight.
Similarly, when Lid joined my party, I teamed her up with Zidane, knowing his Saboteur skills to disrupt and debuff enemies would make Lid a tricky and versatile opponent when combined with her damage dealing Commando skill set.
In short, my characters adapted over time to suit my playstyle, but the game never locked me into taking one specific route for their growth, meaning I could evolve them to match the challenges of my quest. And by collecting magicite during the adventure and visiting the somewhat eccentric Moogle of Light, I could increase the base rank of each Vision and unlock even more abilities.
Of course, Final Fantasy Resonance isn’t just about Visions, even if they’re a crucial part of the game. From its sweeping orchestral score which borrows classic cues from previous titles, to its globe-trotting and occasionally dark tale, there are plenty of traditional elements that will keep fans happy. And yes, you can still whistle for a Chocobo ride, complete with everyone’s favourite theme tune.

The new club can seat 800 people and features an outdoor terrace for plane-spotting as well as two full-service bars and buffets.
The lounge, part of United's $2.6 billion investment at the airport's Terminal B, shows how airlines are putting more money into larger spaces for premium-travel demand to attract the growing ranks of elite frequent flyers, co-branded credit card holders and customers just willing to spend more to fly.
American Airlines earlier this month said it is planning its largest-ever lounge at its Charlotte Douglas International Airport hub in North Carolina. Delta Air Lines has expanded both its popular Delta Sky Clubs and its top-tier Delta One Lounges.
Southwest Airlines is building its first-ever network of airport lounges , which are tied to its credit card partner, Chase . Last week, the carrier unveiled mock-ups of the lounges, which it is calling Icon. And JetBlue Airways opened lounges in New York and Boston in the past year.

By The Maritime Executive 2026-10-20 23:22:44
Commodity intelligence firm Kpler reports that oil flows out of the Arabian Gulf have rebounded so well that they now exceed levels seen before the start of the U.S.-Israel-Iran war. By Kpler's count, the GCC states are now moving about 24 million barrels per day out of the region, including volumes transported by overland pipeline.
The resurgence can be attributed in large part to the U.S.-protected shipping lane through the southern side of the Strait of Hormuz, which is now moving about 14 million barrels per day of crude oil, despite the constant risk of Iranian attack. The hazard level is high, but day rates are as well, and strong earnings have attracted a growing number of tankers in the market despite regular drone and missile strikes. A "Hormuz Shuttle Service" of short-haul tankers provides the backbone, carrying Gulf crude to Fujairah for transfer to other vessels, but there are others as well; TankerTrackers.com counts several hundred ships engaged in various aspects of the trade.
The restoration of Arabian Gulf exports has been done without Iran, which remains cut off by a U.S. Navy blockade. With no sign of progress in peace negotiations, that naval mission is expected to continue. The U.S. Navy flotilla in the Arabian Sea is getting reinforcement soon from the carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt and her escorts, now under way from Japan to the Mideast, U.S. officials confirmed to Fox News' Liz Friden on Tuesday. The Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group - comprised of amphibs USS Makin Island , USS Anchorage and USS John P. Murtha - is also under way from San Diego to join the task force near the Gulf of Oman. articles.title_orig: PHP2Shell: What Actually Protects You Before the 14:00 UTC PHP RCE Patch, and What Doesn't
articles.title_zh: PHP2Shell: What Actually Protects You Before the 14:00 UTC PHP RCE Patch, and What Doesn't
articles.content_orig:
You cannot fully block the two critical PHP flaws called PHP2Shell before today's fix, and the one setting being passed around as a workaround is not enough on its own, the security firm that suggested it now says.
PHP will release the fix at 14:00 UTC on October 21 for two flaws it rates 9.2 out of 10, and has given no workaround of its own. Until you can install it, what lowers your risk is taking exposed PHP off the internet or behind access controls, cutting what a compromised server can reach, and having the update ready to apply the moment it lands.
Cloudflare says it is seeing early attempts to exploit the flaws, and has pushed emergency rules for sites behind it that it calls a stopgap until you patch. No compromise has been confirmed, the public exploit code going around has not been shown to work, and neither flaw is in CISA's catalog of known exploited flaws. PHP has not said which versions are affected, which part of PHP is involved, or whether any setting changes the risk; it says the full details and the fixed versions come with the release.
At the time of writing, that release was not yet out. So nobody outside the group that found the flaws can test whether a given defense works, which is why the advice below is about lowering risk, not promising safety.
The workaround spreading on social media and security blogs is one line in a PHP configuration file: session.upload_progress.enabled=0 . It turns off Session Upload Progress, a PHP feature that's enabled by default, which records how far a file upload has progressed so another request can check on it.
GMO Flatt Security, a Tokyo security firm, suggested setting it early on October 21, saying it could not be sure the change fully addresses the flaws but thought it would help with some probability.
Later the same day, the firm walked that back. In an update timestamped 14:00 Japan time (05:00 UTC), it said the setting alone is not a complete fix and that attacks getting around it are expected. It told administrators to prepare their update, watch for attack traffic before the release, and apply the fix as soon as it is out.
Two people from the PHP project said the same thing more bluntly. Replying to someone who suggested the upload-progress setting might patch the flaw, Gina Peter Banyard, a PHP core developer and documentation writer funded by the PHP Foundation, wrote : "The only thing I can say is that the only mitigation is patching / upgrading PHP. I sadly know too much." Joe Ferguson, the release manager for the coming PHP 8.6, put it shorter : "ini settings won't save you."
The setting cannot be relied on for two reasons. GMO Flatt expects a way around it but has not said what that is. And the whole idea that the flaw lives in Session Upload Progress is a guess: PHP has not confirmed it, the firm itself said it holds only so far as its own research matches PHP2Shell, and an independent code audit argues the specific bug others describe in that feature does not exist in released PHP. That audit is from an anonymous account and PHP's own code will settle it, but it is one more reason not to treat the setting as a shield.
Not everyone agrees. One vendor, Upwind, still lists the setting as an immediate mitigation , passing along another researcher's analysis rather than its own tests. watchTowr, which reproduced one of the flaws, says there is "no confirmed patch or workaround at this time."
No one is telling you to undo the change. The instruction is only not to count it as protection. PHP's own manual already advises turning the feature off where an application does not use upload progress bars, because the stored file names and field names "are not validated and may contain PHP code." If you turned it on by mistake somewhere that needs it, the only cost is that upload progress bars stop working.
Check that the change is actually in effect on the process that serves web traffic, not on the command line. The setting is INI_PERDIR, so it can be set in php.ini, .htaccess, or .user.ini.
A .user.ini file is read only by the CGI and FastCGI versions of PHP, not by the Apache module, and PHP re-reads it only every 300 seconds by default, so a change there can take five minutes to apply.
Under the Apache module, use .htaccess or the server config. Confirm the value on PHP-FPM or mod_php, whichever serves your site, not on php -i at the shell.
Get ready now. GMO Flatt's advice is to confirm your update steps and the checks you run afterward, rehearse any config change, and line up the people and approvals for a possible emergency restart. When the fix lands, update the runtime that serves web requests, which is PHP-FPM, mod_php, or CGI, not the application on top of it.
PHP issues fixes only for its four supported branches, 8.2 through 8.5. Which exact versions carry the fix and how far back the flaws extend will be announced with the release.
The Hacker News reported the branch support and the wider background in its earlier coverage of the disclosure.
Where an immediate update is not possible, CERT-EU advises organizations to "consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix can be applied." Banyard put the same point from inside the project: turning a server off for a day "might be the most sensible thing to do. But that is far from a reasonable thing to demand for most people." Short of shutting down, restrict reach: put the site behind a VPN, allowlisted clients, or authenticated access at the edge, and check that traffic cannot reach the origin directly around those controls.
Shrink what an attacker gets if the server is taken over. GMO Flatt's other steps are to reduce the data stored on the server, reduce its privileges, remove stored credentials, including cloud roles, and ensure logging is enabled and kept in a secure location so you can investigate later.
Branches older than 8.2, including 8.1, 7.x, and 5.x, are end-of-life and receive no PHP fixes. For those, upgrade, take the system offline, or isolate it; a Linux distribution or hosting provider may backport a fix on its own schedule.
A web application firewall is a stopgap here, not a fix, and Cloudflare says so itself. It has pushed emergency rules for the known exploit paths, free tier included, which its CTO calls "a STOPGAP only" ahead of patching. Such rules only see traffic that passes through Cloudflare, and they can miss new attack paths as they appear.
Updating WordPress, Laravel, or another application does not update the PHP runtime underneath it; that comes from your server package, host, or container image. On managed or shared hosting, ask your provider when a fixed PHP build will land and have them stand by.
Hosting providers build their packages only after PHP ships the fix: CloudLinux, for one, says its updated packages depend on the upstream release and will be posted when ready.
Exploitation is early and unconfirmed. Cloudflare reports emerging attempts; watchTowr says it reproduced one flaw but has not reported attacks; the public exploit code going around has not been shown to work; and neither flaw was in CISA's catalog of known exploited flaws when it was last checked on October 21.
A researcher has posted a video said to demonstrate the exploit chain, and the audit above states that the circulating proof-of-concept code does not fire against released PHP. Treat all of this as a snapshot that can change by the hour.
When the fix ships, check the fixed version for your branch, which versions PHP lists as affected, whether PHP confirms or rejects any setting as a mitigation, and whether the session code changed, which also answers the dispute over where the flaw lives.
The fixed versions and the advisory will appear on php.net and through PHP's GitHub security advisories , where the project assigns its own identifiers. After updating, review your logs for anything that happened before you patched.

United States Special Envoy Steve Witkoff has arrived in St Petersburg for talks with Russian leaders on the Ukraine war following “positive” talks with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Norway.
Witkoff is due to meet President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday in the city in northwestern Russia, as the US pushes for an end to the war that began more than four and a half years ago with Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
US President Donald Trump has expressed increasing frustration with Zelenskyy in recent weeks and has suggested that someone else should negotiate on Kyiv’s behalf. The remarks signalled a new low in their relationship, while Zelenskyy has accused the US of suspending crucial intelligence sharing.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described the talks between Witkoff and Zelenskyy as “positive”, adding that the US envoy would share the results with Putin. Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner also attended the talks with Zelenskyy, but did so virtually because of illness. Kushner is also expected to attend the meeting with Putin remotely.
“He’ll now, armed with those ideas, be able to go to St Petersburg and share them with the Russian side – and let’s see if we can make some progress,” Rubio said.
The prime ministers of Norway and Finland also attended the talks in Oslo. Representatives from the European Union and NATO were present. Following Tuesday’s talks, Zelenskyy said “very, very important” intelligence from the US had been restored.
Zelenskyy has also accused Washington of slowing down the internet service, Starshield, which is crucial for Ukraine’s battlefield operations. Starshield is the military-grade equivalent of Starlink and is also developed by Elon Musk’s SpaceX.
Rubio dismissed Zelenskyy’s accusations, saying Trump had “nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield”. Musk disputes this and says such decisions can only be made by the US military and president.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday that Musk ordered the slowdown of the service, citing US officials and people familiar ⁠with the matter.
As diplomatic efforts intensify, Russia and Ukraine continue to trade long-range attacks.
At least one person was killed and two were wounded in a Ukrainian drone attack in Russia’s western Bryansk ⁠region on Wednesday, Governor Yegor Kovalchuk said on Telegram.

articles.title_orig: Russian prime minister says Russia-China trade turnover grows more than 30-fold over 25 years
articles.title_zh: Russian prime minister says Russia-China trade turnover grows more than 30-fold over 25 years
articles.content_orig:
Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin said on Wednesday that trade turnover between Russia and China has increased more than 30-fold over the past 25 years despite external pressure.
Speaking at a meeting in St. Petersburg with Chinese Premier Li Qiang ahead of the 31st regular meeting between the two countries' heads of government, Mishustin added that bilateral trade was growing steadily, with nearly all transactions conducted in national currencies, the ruble and the yuan.
"Despite increased external pressure, Russia-China trade and economic cooperation has demonstrated strong momentum: over the past 25 years, our bilateral trade turnover has increased more than 30-fold," he said.
More than 90 projects across various sectors, from metallurgy to agriculture, are currently in the portfolio of the relevant bilateral commission, Mishustin said.
"Today, the share of national currencies in bilateral trade is already close to 100%," the Russian prime minister said, adding that bilateral investment was also increasing.
Mishustin called China a key economic partner, pledged continued reliable energy supplies, cited peaceful nuclear projects as a promising area, and noted that Russia remains China's top oil supplier with Power of Siberia -- the gas conduit stretching from Siberia to China -- running steadily.
"Russia will continue to reliably ensure uninterrupted energy supplies. We are also ready to strengthen cooperation in the energy sector," he said.
Bilateral agricultural trade grew by more than one-third in the first nine months of 2026 compared with the same period last year, Mishustin said.
Russian products marketed under the Made in Russia brand had demonstrated their quality and were gaining popularity in China, he added.
The two countries should expand the range of goods traded between them to meet consumer demand, the Russian prime minister said.
Mutual tourist flows between Russia and China increased by approximately 50% in the first half of 2026, Mishustin said. He also called for more active modernization of border crossing points and an expansion of the geographical reach of air transport links between the countries.
Li Qiang said Russian-Chinese relations entered a new stage of more substantive and accelerated development under the strategic leadership of Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
He described the regular meeting as an important opportunity to comprehensively review bilateral cooperation, address existing issues and translate agreements reached by the leaders into practical action and tangible results for their peoples.
Li said that despite changes in the international situation over recent decades, the two countries' commitment to good-neighborly relations, friendship, cooperation and development had remained unchanged.
"Adhering to the principles of non-alignment, non-confrontation and not targeting third parties, we have upheld mutual respect and mutually beneficial cooperation," he said, adding that Russia and China had established a model of high-level mutual trust and cooperation between major powers and neighboring countries.
The regular meeting between the Russian and Chinese heads of government is being held for the 31st time. The previous meeting took place in China in early November 2025, in Hangzhou and Beijing.

articles.title_orig: Australian politician who was hit by car has lost both legs
articles.title_zh: Australian politician who was hit by car has lost both legs
articles.content_orig:
Australian federal lawmaker Helen Haines had had both legs amputated after a driver allegedly rammed her repeatedly on Monday outside her electorate office, her husband says
MELBOURNE, Australia -- Doctors have amputated both of Australian federal lawmaker Helen Haines ' legs as she remains in critical condition after being repeatedly hit by a car in an apparent act of political violence, her husband said Wednesday.
The 65-year-old independent politician is receiving treatment in a Melbourne hospital where she was flown by helicopter.
Phil Haines, her husband, gave the family’s first public comments on her condition since she was hit by a Toyota Land Cruiser SUV in her hometown of Wangaratta on Monday, speaking hours after a man accused of running her over made an initial appearance in court.
Haines' husband said her left leg was amputated on Monday and her right leg was amputated on Wednesday after doctors abandoned hope of saving it.
“The good news in all this is that Helen is alive and she’s stable. That is the most important thing for our family,” the husband told reporters in Melbourne.
“We are grateful and thankful that at this stage, both her heart and her mind are in good shape,” he said.
He added that their 40th wedding anniversary will be in November.
Earlier Wednesday, Brendan Nugent, a 43-year-old man from nearby Tarrawingee, appeared in the Wangaratta Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday charged with intentionally causing serious injury, dangerous driving causing serious injury and causing harm to a federal official.
Nugent didn’t apply for bail or enter a plea. He will remain in custody until his next court appearance in February. Police have yet to determine a motive.
Nugent's lawyer Chirag Patel told Magistrate Allison Vaughan that his client was suffering from potential mental health issues and a concussion. The lawyer did not explain how Nugent had been concussed.
Patel said Nugent suffered from a neurological condition, idiopathic transverse myelitis, but had not been diagnosed with any mental health problems.
The rare condition damages the spinal cord’s protective myelin sheath and disrupts nerve signals between the brain and body. This leads to rapid muscle weakness, sensory loss, pain, and bladder and bowel dysfunction, according to the Cleveland Clinic medical center.
Witnesses say the driver rammed his victim, pinning her against her own car before reversing and ramming her a second time.
The well-regarded lawmaker's plight has shocked Australians, as political violence is uncommon in the country and politicians are highly accessible to the public. Most lawmakers are not accompanied by security details and go about their work and personal lives on their own.
Senior opposition lawmaker James Paterson on Wednesday called for a review of lawmakers’ personal security in response to the alleged crime.
“The reality is that Australian parliamentarians by global standards are uniquely accessible to the public and that’s a good thing,” Paterson told Australian Broadcasting Corp.
“But we … can’t have a situation where shocking attacks like this take place because that will fundamentally change our democracy forever if it becomes a serious risk to your life to be a member of parliament,” Paterson added.
But Prime Minister Anthony Albanese urged lawmakers to continue to engage openly with the public despite worsening animosity within the community.
“We want to make sure that people can feel as much comfort as possible that everything’s being done to maximize security,” Albanese told News24.
“I think parliamentarians across the board are determined to make sure that we can continue to engage as we need to in this great democracy of ours,” Albanese added. “That interaction is really important in our democracy.”
Graham-McLay reported from Wellington, New Zealand.

articles.content_orig:
China has all the signs of world-topping national strength but whether other countries accept its leadership will depend on what’s on offer
As turbulence grows in many countries, it is tempting to ask if there is a global hegemon that can sort everything out fairly.
Our latest projections of national strength for 2027 take into account resources, territory, economic strength and military power. They still put China in first place, with its lead over other countries widening. But when might China move beyond leading the ranking to exert decisive influence over the world’s trouble spots and become a global arbiter?
To explore that question, we should first look at how states have assessed national power. Ancient rulers counted people, revenues, troops, ships and resources but these were separate assessments, not a single measure of national power.

articles.content_orig:
U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff is holding talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin about ending the war in Ukraine, a day after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy insisted that any negotiations over his country's future must include Kyiv.
Speaking alongside the leaders of Finland and Norway in Oslo late on Tuesday, Zelenskyy said discussions with U.S. officials had been constructive and that Washington had reaffirmed its commitment to providing Ukraine with security guarantees.
But he stressed that any agreement concerning Ukraine's future would be acceptable only if Kyiv had a seat at the negotiating table.
"It can be acceptable only when we are at the table of negotiations," he said, adding that he had discussed the reported proposal of a trilateral meeting between the U.S., China, and Russia to negotiate an end to the almost five-year conflict with U.S. representatives. "Nothing about Ukraine without Ukraine," he said.
At the start of talks in St. Petersburg, Russia announced it would release an American man who had been "wrongfully detained," according to the State Department, on charges that he was a Ukrainian mercenary. Witkoff thanked Putin for the release of retired teacher Stephen Hubbard, according to Russian media .
On Tuesday, Zelenskyy said the Oslo meeting had included discussions on NATO's Article 5 – which says that an armed attack against one member constitutes an attack on all – and "different kinds of security guarantees," which Witkoff will share with the Russians. "We will hear his feedback in one day," Zelenskyy said Tuesday.
The developments come amid heightened tensions between the U.S. and Ukraine as President Donald Trump and Zelenskyy have traded public criticism. Trump has accused the Ukrainian president of not wanting peace, while Zelenskyy has argued that Washington's easing of sanctions on Russia, including a deal on diesel , risks prolonging the conflict.
Overnight, Russia struck energy and civilian targets across Ukraine, resulting in at least one casualty, according to local media reports. It follows Trump's Oct. 11 claim that he had brokered an "energy ceasefire," whereby the countries would refrain from striking each other's energy infrastructure amid high diesel prices.
Ukraine paused such attacks for three days before resuming them, citing continuing Russian attacks.
On Tuesday, Zelenskyy confirmed that U.S. intelligence had resumed sharing early warnings of Russian attacks, while discussions continued over SpaceX's Starlink connectivity and Patriot air defense systems.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told CNBC's Phil LeBeau that safety is paramount, but he also said the U.S. needs to improve its certification process.
"It takes Boeing, to certify an aircraft in Europe, about half the time, less than half the time that it does in the U.S. You have China now playing to take over in aviation," Duffy said. "We have to certify aircraft more quickly if we're going to compete as Americans."
The 737 Max 10, the largest model in the family that can seat up to 230 people, was set to start flying in 2020, but increased scrutiny following two Max crashes in 2018 and 2019 and other safety issues delayed its certification. Engineering changes were also required, including to an anti-icing system for the aircraft's engines.
Max 10 customers include Alaska Airlines , American Airlines , United Airlines and Delta Air Lines . Boeing said the Max 10 makes up about 30% of its Max backlog.
Airlines can finally start flying passengers soon after planes are certified, but it can take months for carriers to work them into schedules.
"Completing the certification program clears the path for us to deliver a Boeing airplane that will set a new standard in commercial aviation," Stephanie Pope, CEO of Boeing's commercial airplane unit, said in a news release.
United CEO Scott Kirby told CNBC in August that the airline had been waiting so long for the Max 10 that the lie-flat seats it expected for the plane no longer make sense and are sitting in a warehouse. Alaska Airlines last month said it plans to put lie-flat seats on some of its 737 Max 10s in a push for more premium offerings.
The FAA approved the smallest model of the 737 Max family, the Max 7 , in early August.
Boeing has been working to ramp up production of its 737 Maxes and 787 Dreamliners, which are key to its recovery since airlines and other customers pay the bulk of the aircraft's price upon delivery. The manufacturer opened a fourth production line in Everett, Washington, in July for its 737 Max airplanes.

articles.title_orig: China, Russia Deepen Arctic Ties as Japan, Iceland Boost Science Cooperation
articles.title_zh: China, Russia Deepen Arctic Ties as Japan, Iceland Boost Science Cooperation
articles.content_orig:
(Stock image/Russian flag, from Pixabay)
Two senior fellows from the Sasakawa Peace Foundation, Natsuhiko Otsuka and Hiroyuki Enomoto, spoke at the Arctic Circle Assembly, held in Reykjavik, Iceland, from October 8 to 10.
Speaking on October 8, Otsuka highlighted growing cooperation between China and Russia to develop Arctic shipping routes and examined the broader international implications of a new Arctic cooperation framework proposed by Moscow.
On October 10, Enomoto discussed the growing collaboration between Japanese and Icelandic scientists in Arctic research. He also emphasized the importance of "science diplomacy" as the two countries mark the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations.
Otsuka said China is "becoming a major power on the Arctic sea route," citing the rapid expansion of NewNew Shipping Line, a Chinese container shipping company established in 2022. Initially focused on shipping to Russia, the company has recently expanded its operations to include exports to Europe via the Arctic.
According to Otsuka, the company can afford the route's commercial risks because it expects "substantial cargo demand for Arctic shipping." One possible explanation is that its parent company handles shipments for both Chinese exporters and Chinese importers operating in Europe.
This gives NewNew Shipping Line an advantage, as it faces little price competition from major international shipping companies.
Japanese and South Korean shipping firms, however, face a different set of challenges. Given the geopolitical risks associated with Russia, Otsuka said it is not easy for carriers in either country to find domestic customers willing to ship goods along the Arctic route off Russia's northern coast.
On freight rates, Otsuka said the Arctic route would struggle to compete with the lower costs offered by ultra-large container ships passing through the Suez Canal.
Russia, meanwhile, faces significant challenges in developing the Arctic route. Its cargo volume targets are overly ambitious, while international isolation following its invasion of Ukraine has further complicated its plans.
Given these challenges, Otsuka said China's growing use of the route provides a much-needed boost to Russia's ambitions.
At an international conference hosted in September, Russia proposed a new framework for Arctic cooperation, seeking an alternative to the existing Arctic Council, whose seven other members continue to impose sanctions on Moscow.
Otsuka warned that the proposal could divide the region into two competing blocs: the "Arctic Seven" and a Russia-led group of sympathetic non-Arctic countries.
The Arctic Seven comprise the United States, Canada, Denmark, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, and Finland—all NATO members. Otsuka said the proposal could deepen tensions between NATO members in the Arctic and countries aligned with Russia.
For now, Otsuka described the prospect of establishing a new international body to rival the Arctic Council as being at an "uncertain conceptual stage."
However, he noted that growing cooperation between China and Russia on Arctic shipping is already producing tangible results. He suggested this cooperation could be a "practical step" toward establishing a new Russia-led international organization.
Speaking at a separate session, Enomoto thanked Icelandic government officials and university researchers for their contributions to growing scientific cooperation between Japan and Iceland.
Japan gained observer status on the Arctic Council in 2013 and has since strengthened its ties with Iceland through initiatives such as the Arctic Science Ministerial and the first Arctic Circle Tokyo Forum, held in 2023.
Iceland's ambassador to Japan, Hreinn Pálsson, echoed Enomoto's remarks, emphasizing the importance of science diplomacy in bilateral relations.
He also expressed hope that continued cooperation between Japanese and Icelandic scientists would help further strengthen ties between the two countries.

articles.title_orig: 60 years on: The Aberfan disaster through the eyes of those who survived
articles.title_zh: 60 years on: The Aberfan disaster through the eyes of those who survived
articles.content_orig:
Few events have left a deeper mark on Wales than the Aberfan disaster.
Sixty years on , the tragedy remains woven into the nation's collective memory, a day of unimaginable loss that reshaped a community and changed attitudes to industrial safety across Britain.
At 09:15 on 21 October 1966, an ordinary school morning was shattered when a coal tip above Aberfan collapsed.
Black slurry thundered down the mountainside, engulfing Pantglas Junior School and nearby homes. Within moments, 144 people were dead, including 116 children, on what was the last day of school before the half term holiday.
On the 60th anniversary, those who were there share their harrowing memories.
"What I remember was the drizzly rain, it was misty. I rang the bell to start school at about ten to nine, before the children went in.
"There was this terrible noise, and I looked out of the window. I could see a wall had collapsed and realised I had to get my pupils outside.
"As we escaped, I saw the caretaker rushing to get other children out.
"They opened Bethania Chapel to take children who had died, but the first bodies were placed in a shelter in the playground.
"We identified them before they were cleaned up, and before their parents were told.
"I found that very hard. I remember one little girl, I can see her face now.
"She had beautiful black curly hair."
"There was this really unusual sound, like a rumble. Like if you chuck stones across the floor, but it was getting louder and louder.
"Next thing, water was seeping through the floor, the walls were cracking and timbers were breaking.
"The teacher put a desk on a table, and a small chair on top of that. She climbed on top and smashed the window.
"And then she held us up, probably by the scruffs of our necks, to get us out through it.
"I am so grateful for her quick thinking, she saved our lives.
"When I got outside, I could see a mountain of coal and slurry, with dust and water everywhere.
"I ran home, and remember saying: 'Mam, mam, the mountain came down to the school'."
"I heard this tremendous sound, like a hurricane. It was so overwhelming, I knew something was coming, but didn't know what.
"Then this mass of black came crashing through the window, hurling me from the front of the classroom to the back.
"I woke up to find the classroom was no longer the classroom. The roof had caved in on us, and we were completely buried.
"I couldn't see my legs, I thought they had gone.
"A pupil in front of me was trapped, and he had blood trickling down his head. Another one was trying to get through the roof to get help.
"My head was cut open, and I couldn't move my hand as it was stuck in the cracked wall.
"I pinched the hand of a child near me to see if it would move. It didn't.
"Then I heard someone shout 'I'm going to smash the window' and saw my grandfather.
"I started to cry and will never forget the look in his eyes knowing I was alive.
"I'd broken my femur, my leg was just swinging and my shoes had gone.
"'I'll buy you all the shoes you need,' my mum said as she greeted me outside.
"My parents then ran off to find my siblings.
"I was later told Carl and Marylyn had died, and all my friends had gone as well.
"My life changed forever."
"As the teacher spoke by the blackboard, there was a rumbling sound that got louder and louder.
"The lights started to sway back and fore, but the teacher reassured us there was nothing to worry about. It was only thunder.
"The next thing I remember was waking up and seeing light from the sky because the roof had come in.
"I was stuck but awake and could see a dead girl on my shoulder.
"There was screaming, shouting and crying, but this got less and less."
"This was because the children were dying of physical trauma, the roof and slurry coming in, or they couldn't breathe, they had no air.
"I was lucky because I had this balloon of air around me.
"The fire service broke through the window from the hall, and somebody saw my white hair.
"They started digging and eventually they got me out, passing me in a chain from one fireman to another.
"I got out just after 11, and was the last child to come out alive.
"Tom Harding, the local grocer, threw me in his van with the cabbages and the carrots, and took me to St Tydfil's Hospital."
"I was at my desk, quite close to the western side of the school that took the fullest impact.
"Almost immediately I was engulfed with debris and falling masonry, which knocked me unconscious.
"I'm told I was brought out and placed with the deceased bodies and covered with a blanket.
"Then someone thought they saw my foot move.
"The doctor re-examined me.
"I was evidently still alive and taken to hospital."
"After having pneumonia, I almost stayed at home - but was determined to go in for the last day.
"I looked out of the window towards the tip and told my teacher I could see smoke.
"He said it was just steam from the canteen, which I thought was odd, because there was no canteen in the infants school - that was in the senior school.
"But it was coming closer and closer.
"I put my head on the desk with my book over it - I don't know why, it was just instinct.
"The next thing I knew, I woke up and I was under coal, soil and muck.
"When I tried to breathe, I just sucked water in and I had coal waste over my face.
"There was lots of crying and screaming, then it went black again.
"When I woke up, there was silence, nobody crying, and the little boy next to me was dead.
"One of my classmates was walking around and he helped dig me out.
"In the hallway, there was a queue of children waiting to be pulled out of the window by a teacher.
"There was one boy stood there and he just wouldn't move, he was stunned.
"I was pulled out and never knew what happened to him.
"Then I found out years later he'd died of a heart attack before being rescued."
"I can remember being very, very close to her. She used to do things like comb my hair. I had great hopes for her.
"We had breakfast, I went to work and Anne went to school.
"It was absolute chaos there - people trying to get into the school.
"There was hope in my mind they may find her. I was walking the roads until 10 at night, just living in hope.
"I didn't know for certain she'd died until I saw her in the mortuary in Bethania Chapel.
"It's hard to think about it now.
I'd like to have known her for that bit longer, because the eight years went very quickly."
"A neighbour knocked on my door and he was in a terrible state, shaking like a leaf.
"He wanted to use my phone to call the fire brigade because a house on Moy Road had collapsed.
"As we talked, a lady ran past shouting: 'The school has gone, the school has gone.'
"I ran down the road and was taken aback - the houses on Moy Road were concertinaed.
"A child was shouting 'help me, help me' from under the rubble.
"People were going to him, so I headed for the school.
"Lorries were arriving, each with about 40 miners from Merthyr Vale colliery who had shovels and pickaxes.
"There were bereaved mothers, and I thought 'What the hell has happened?'
"Policemen were carrying stretchers with body bags on them, and I thought to myself, 'where is God? How did he allow this to happen with all these children?'"
"I had been on the bus through Aberfan when somebody shouted 'the school has fallen down'.
"I remember thinking 'that sounds a bit silly', but looked up and there was a gap.
"If you've ever seen photos, it [the slurry] took the junior school, but left the senior school completely free.
"I was thinking something's not right, but then your journalistic brain kicks into gear, and I realised I had work to do.
"Not as something you want to do, but it's your job."
"You could just about see the top of the school, but it was totally engulfed by this black mass.
"Men worked with shovels, their hands, desperately trying to find survivors.
"Every so often, a whistle blew and everybody stopped working.

articles.title_orig: PHP2Shell: Two Unpatched Critical PHP RCE Flaws (CVSS 9.2) Trigger Emergency Security Alert
articles.title_zh: PHP2Shell: Two Unpatched Critical PHP RCE Flaws (CVSS 9.2) Trigger Emergency Security Alert
articles.content_orig:
This story is developing and was written before PHP's scheduled 14:00 UTC release on October 21. Once the release is out, the affected and fixed versions below are confirmed by the official advisory.
PHP will ship an out-of-cycle security release at 14:00 UTC today, October 21, for two critical vulnerabilities that its security team has rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 scale but has not described.
Security researchers at watchTowr say the two flaws allow remote code execution. Only the four supported PHP branches, 8.2 through 8.5, can receive the fix, and no exploitation has been reported so far.
The advance notice followed a leak. On October 20, a post on HN said two PHP remote code execution flaws, rated CVSS 10.0 and affecting versions from PHP 5 onward, would be disclosed on Thursday, October 22. The poster said they had "no evidence beyond 'source: trust me, bro'".
watchTowr then posted on X that the leaked information was real, that the two flaws were under embargo, that everyone had been supposed to wait until Thursday, and that it could not share more for now.
PHP published its notice that evening, at 19:33 UTC, with the release set for Wednesday, a day before the date watchTowr gave. The notice says PHP may release earlier "should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild."
The leak carried the flaws' existence, a score, a date, and two CVE identifiers, not how the flaws work. The CVSS 10.0 figure is the leak's. PHP's rating is 9.2 on version 4.0 of the scale.
The identifiers researchers are using, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 , were also listed in the leaked post. PHP's notice names neither. The claim that every version since PHP 5 is affected is unconfirmed too: watchTowr's own FAQ on the flaws says that scope "has not been confirmed by an official vendor advisory" and that no configuration or feature requirement has been described.
PHP says "Full details, affected versions, and the fixed versions will be published with the release." Researchers have started calling the pair php2shell. The name is theirs, not PHP's.
Whatever the affected range turns out to be, PHP issues fixes only for its four supported branches , and records each branch's changes in its changelog . Versions 8.2 and 8.3 receive only security fixes, and 8.4 and 8.5 are in active support. Ahead of the release, several trackers, including Alpine Linux's and security researcher Kevin Beaumont, expect the fixes to ship as PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, the next point release of each branch, though PHP has not confirmed the numbers.
Anything older, including 8.1, 8.0, 7.x, and 5.x, is end of life and gets no PHP fix. If the flaws reach those branches, installations on them will have no vendor patch.
Security company Mallory counted about 884,000 internet-facing hosts whose HTTP banner reported a PHP version of 8.1 or older to the Shodan search engine on October 20, 59% of the roughly 1.5 million hosts that reported any version. The count covers banners, not confirmed affected systems, and a further 740,000 hosts reported PHP without a version.
PHP has published no workaround. Until the release lands, the preparation comes down to six steps, most of them drawn from a rapid-response post from Huntress , with CERT-EU's isolation advice added.
Huntress said it had not seen exploitation of the flaws in its partner environments as of October 20, had not built or reproduced a proof of concept, and was not aware of public exploit code. watchTowr's FAQ lists exploitation as none reported as of October 21 and the flaws as not in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
For comparison, when CVE-2024-4577 , a PHP flaw in CGI mode on Windows, became public in June 2024, Akamai saw exploit attempts against its honeypot servers within 24 hours.
The release should clarify what the notice withheld: which versions are affected, which part of PHP is involved, whether an attack requires a particular way of running PHP, a configuration, or a login, and how PHP itself describes the flaws. At the time of writing, PHP had not released the fixes.

articles.title_zh: China says it is 'safeguarding order' around Taiwan-controlled South China Sea atoll
articles.content_orig:
BEIJING, Oct 21 (Reuters) - China's government said on Wednesday that its coast guard was "safeguarding order" around a tiny and strategically located Taiwan-controlled atoll at the top end of the ‌South China Sea where Taipei fears Beijing is trying to enforce jurisdiction.
China, which views democratically governed ‌Taiwan as its own territory, said last week that Taiwan must "bear the consequences" of its coast guard using a water cannon ​against a Chinese fishing boat near the Pratas Islands.
Taiwan has reported two incidents since Sunday of Chinese coast guard vessels approaching the Pratas, accusing Beijing of provocative behaviour.
Speaking at a regular news briefing, a spokesperson for China's Taiwan Affairs Office said Beijing has "indisputable sovereignty" over the South China Sea islands, including the Pratas and ‌their adjacent waters.
"Mainland coast guard vessels conducting ⁠law enforcement patrols in the relevant waters are fulfilling their duties in accordance with the law, safeguarding normal navigation and operational order," spokesperson Zhang Han told reporters.
The ⁠Chinese ships are "effectively protecting the lawful and legitimate rights and interests of people on both sides of the Taiwan Strait and the safety of lives and property", she added.
The "obstinate insistence" by Taiwan's ruling party on its separatist ​stance is ​the root cause of the peril of war across ​the strait, Zhang said.
Taiwan's government rejects Beijing's ‌territorial claims, saying only the Taiwanese people can decide their future.
China recognises no claims of sovereignty by Taiwan and has never renounced the use of force to bring the island under its control.
The Pratas have no permanent civilian population and lie roughly between southern Taiwan and Hong Kong. Security experts see them as vulnerable to Chinese attack due to their distance — more than 400 km (250 miles) — from Taiwan.
China's military ‌already operates around Taiwan on an almost daily basis. Taipei has ​become increasingly alarmed by Beijing's use of its coast guard to ​carry out "law enforcement" patrols to try to ​assert jurisdiction.
Addressing a forum in Taipei late Tuesday, Taiwan's top China-policy maker said Beijing ‌is attempting to "domesticate" the Taiwan issue to "create an ​illusion of having de ​facto jurisdiction over Taiwan's surrounding waters and offshore islands".
With President Xi Jinping expected to be confirmed for a fourth term in office next year, China's mission to "achieve national unification" becomes even more ​pressing, said Chiu Chui-cheng, head of ‌the Mainland Affairs Council.
"We assess that Beijing's Taiwan policy will shift toward a more aggressive, ​provocative strategy of 'exercising jurisdiction before achieving unification'," he added.
(Reporting by Beijing newsroom; Additional reporting ​by Ben Blanchard in Taipei; Editing by Lincoln Feast.)

articles.title_zh: PHP Warns of Two Critical 9.2 Security Vulnerabilities, Urges Users to Prepare for Patches
articles.content_orig:
Website admins, brace yourselves. Fixes for what are believed to be uncommonly severe vulnerabilities are scheduled to drop in a little more than 12 hours for PHP, a programming language that powers websites and Web applications everywhere.
PHP maintainers said Monday that they planned to release patches for two vulnerabilities, both with severity ratings of 9.2 out of a possible 10.
“All PHP users are encouraged to prepare now so they can upgrade as soon as the release is available,” the advisory stated. “We reserve the right to release earlier should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild.”
The maintainers published the advisory following the leaking of purported details, which have yet to be confirmed. The report showed a video of an exploit tool dubbed PHP2Shell executing code on webservers running WordPress 7.1.3, MediaWiki 1.46.2, phpBB 3.3.17, Magento 2.4.9, Joomla 6.2.0, Laravel 13.36.0, Laravel 8.83.29, Symphony 8.1.9, Drupal 11.4.10, and WHMCS 9.0.9, all of which use PHP. A video depicting the tool has been reposted here .
Attempts to locate the unconfirmed report were unsuccessful, but security firm watchTowr said it claimed to affect every PHP version from PHP 5, released in 2004, onward. The security firm went on to say it has confirmed that the vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are real.
Researchers from separate security firm Sansec said they “expect mass attacks to start within 15 minutes of the release.” A third security firm, Webfence, also urged admins to prepare now. Huntress has also issued an advisory.
Preparation steps include identifying who is responsible for managing PHP inside an organization, taking an inventory of every app built on the language, planning a maintenance window starting at 14:00 UTC with contingency plans for earlier, making a backup of site and database files, and monitoring the PHP.net homepage for any late-breaking announcements, including an earlier release time. Some experts suggest unplugging any non-essential systems until they’re patched.
As an open source scripting language for building dynamic websites and web apps, PHP has come to be a de facto building block for the Web. It runs multiple CMS apps in addition to WordPress and also powers many internal tools. One security researcher said an estimated 1.3 million Internet-connected hosts are likely affected. Vulnerabilities with the severity the advisories are describing have the potential to inflict major damage across the Internet. Admins should remain aware that the patches can be released at any moment and remain vigilant until they do.

articles.title_orig: Scientists discover ghostly, eyeless creature hidden in Chinese cave
articles.title_zh: Scientists discover ghostly, eyeless creature hidden in Chinese cave
articles.content_orig:
A newly identified freshwater cave snail in China is offering scientists a rare glimpse into the little-known aquatic ecosystems hidden beneath East Asia. Published in the journal Subterranean Biology , the discovery represents an important step forward in understanding the region's underground wildlife. Until now, no freshwater cave snails had been documented in China, and the country's subterranean freshwater mollusks had received relatively little scientific attention.
The newly discovered species, Erhaia dijiang , has evolved remarkable features that allow it to live in complete darkness. As a true cave-dwelling animal, it has entirely lost its eyes, with the structures normally associated with vision having fully degenerated. The tiny snail also has a cone-shaped, nearly transparent shell, a delicate body without pigmentation, and long, slender tentacles.
Its unusual appearance inspired a name drawn from ancient Chinese mythology. Researchers chose dijiang in honor of "Di Jiang," a mountain patron god portrayed as a faceless beast in the ancient text Classic of Mountains and Seas (山海经). The connection is particularly fitting because the snail is extremely sensitive to light. During laboratory observations, individuals consistently retreated into dark spaces beneath rocks whenever they were exposed to illumination.
The location of the discovery is just as remarkable as the animal itself. Scientists found Erhaia dijiang at an elevation of 2,062 meters, making it the highest-altitude cave snail yet recorded within the family Erhaiidae. The finding demonstrates that freshwater cave snails can inhabit limestone cave systems at elevations above 2,000 meters.
Life in the Dark Waters of a Mountain Cave
Within its underground habitat, Erhaia dijiang lives among submerged gravel and broken rock in water less than one meter deep. The cave's water temperature stays close to 20°C, providing a relatively stable environment for the tiny mollusks.
Even when heavy seasonal rains increase the flow of water and occasionally wash a few snails out through the cave opening, they have not been observed in nearby streams. Researchers found that the animals remain confined to the cave environment, staying within two meters of its entrance.
Laboratory observations also provided clues about what these elusive creatures eat. The snails were seen feeding on diatoms, microscopic algae that grow on rock surfaces, and they also consumed fish food supplied by the researchers.
Only Three Living Snails Found, Raising Conservation Concerns
Although the discovery sheds new light on China's largely unexplored underground aquatic biodiversity, researchers are concerned about the species' future. They describe its conservation outlook as "far from optimistic."
During the first field investigation in August 2025, the team encountered an exceptionally small number of snails. Despite searching the shallow cave waters, researchers located only three living adults and one empty shell. They found no juveniles, suggesting that the known population is extremely sparse.
The scientists are now urging more comprehensive investigations of cave ecosystems throughout China to uncover additional species and better understand these fragile underground habitats. They also emphasize the need to develop conservation protections quickly for these vulnerable mollusks, which are native to highly restricted environments and could face serious threats before their populations are fully understood.

articles.title_zh: Opinion | Burnham’s Britain can learn from Trump in engaging with China
articles.content_orig:
While an IPAC report accurately notes that Britain is woefully unprepared to get relations with China right, the audit’s ideological framing is unhelpful
Getting relations with China right is widely seen as Britain’s epoch-defining challenge. It is also one it is woefully unprepared to face.
So concluded a recent audit by the Inter-Parliamentary Alliance on China (IPAC), which highlighted that top negotiators lacked basic Chinese language skills. More critically, it exposed a deeper deficit: a poor grasp of China spanning political elites and the public alike. This is rooted in a desk-bound classroom sinology rather than a nuanced appreciation and lived immersion.
Yet IPAC’s audit will do little to fix this deficit. Indeed, its ideological framing will deepen it.
The report depicts China as a neo-totalitarian state seeking to engineer the souls of its citizens. It alleges that this coercive ambition extends globally, that Beijing seeks to upend the liberal world order to usher in an era favourable to authoritarian imperialism.

articles.title_zh: 296 km/h: Super Typhoon Champi is now the strongest storm on Earth in 2026
articles.content_orig:
Super Typhoon Champi has now grown into the world’s strongest tropical cyclone of 2026, with respect to wind speed.
The system in the western Pacific Ocean became a powerhouse with its peak winds of of 296 km/h, the equivalent of a Category 5 storm.
Hurricane Polo previously held the title for world’s strongest tropical cyclone in 2026, in terms of wind speed. The storm peaked with maximum, sustained winds of 285 km/h and a minimum, central pressure of 892 mb--which is still lower than Champi's (895 mb)--making Polo stronger in that regard.
Such a low air pressure made Polo the second-most intense hurricane on record in the eastern Pacific.
Champi is also now the world’s seventh Category 5 storm of the year.

The typhoon also had a very healthy structure on radar as it passed Guam early Sunday morning local time.
Sea surface temperatures in this section of the western Pacific are running around 30°C , which is slightly warmer than normal for this time of year. The environment around the typhoon features deep moisture, calm winds, low wind shear. and enough upper-level support to vent air away from the storm.
The massive Champi will continue to track west towards Taipei before turning northwest later this week.
It will enter a more unfavourable environment, so Champi is forecast to weaken to a Category 4 or 3 storm by Thursday and Friday.
All of those ingredients, plus the storm’s own internal organization, are critical for a tropical cyclone to maintain its composure and continue strengthening.
The massive storm is tugging on the jet stream, having an influence on weather patterns across the globe.
Champi took a more westerly track towards Taiwan. Downstream, impacts to Canada are expected , reinforcing an end-of-October and early-November pattern we have previously been forecasting.
In Ontario and Quebec, the weather is expected to become more changeable and unsettled at times during the middle of and late next week, lingering into the following week.
Warmer-than-normal temperatures are expected to dominate, but quick interruptions are also expected.

Instead, in the run-up to the merger’s completion, Ellison added to a multibillion-dollar borrowing spree. articles.title_zh: Through Chinese eyes: a CASS scholar on Britain’s Xi Jinping Thought Study Group
articles.content_orig:
The following article by Zhuo Mingliang, Associate Research Fellow at the Academy of Marxism of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS), examines the work of the Xi Jinping Thought Study Group, set up in 2020 by the London-based Institute for Independence Studies . Among its founders is our co-editor Keith Bennett.
Zhuo introduces the Study Group and its core members, and summarises the main arguments of its 2023 book of memoirs by long-standing friends of China. These include the view that China’s achievements demonstrate the superiority of socialism, and that Xi Jinping Thought is “a great gift to all humanity” that can help unite progressive forces worldwide. He also outlines the Institute’s distinctive positions, among them its emphasis on the non-Western development of scientific socialism and its critique of Western leftists who remain sceptical of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The article offers an interesting insight into how Chinese scholars view the work of China’s friends in the West – and into the role of people-to-people movements in breaking through the anti-China consensus in the Western media.
The article was originally published in Chinese in the Journal of Handan University (Vol. 36, No. 3, September 2026). The English translation is by Friends of Socialist China; quotations from Keith Bennett’s preface are translated back from the Chinese and will not match his original wording.
Abstract: The “Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era Study Group” is an academic research organisation set up by left-wing British scholars who know China well and are friendly towards it. Writing from the standpoint of overseas people with first-hand experience, its members affirm the international influence of Xi Jinping Thought. They recognise the superiority of the socialist system as shown by China’s development path, and they rebut false anti-China narratives in the West.
Western non-governmental groups that know China and are friendly to it are an important force for breaking down US and Western media bias against China. The article therefore recommends four lines of work:
The aim is to use civil-society forces to “tell China’s story well”, grow a friendly international climate of opinion towards China, and strengthen the popular basis for people-to-people ties between China and other countries.
Keywords: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era; Britain’s Institute for Independence Studies; scientific socialism
At present, British people who know and are friendly towards China follow China’s achievements in reform and development closely. They actively study Xi Jinping Thought, Chinese modernisation, China’s global initiatives and “Chinese solutions”. In doing so they have helped improve mutual understanding between the Chinese and British peoples and helped the international community see China objectively and fairly.
One of these is the “Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era Study Group”. It is an important academic body under the Institute for Independence Studies, and it works to study and spread Xi Jinping Thought in Britain and around the world. It has published a book, Paths to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era: Memoirs of Long-Standing Friends of China and Solidarity Activists . Its views and positions deserve our close attention.
The Institute for Independence Studies is an independent body based in London, founded by left-wing scholars from several countries. It is dedicated to researching and spreading the ideas of social and national liberation, and to applying them to social reality in the era of imperialism. This work is carried out especially through the writings and activities of Keith Bennett.
In August 2020 the Institute set up the Study Group. Its purpose is to study and spread Xi Jinping Thought, to draw from it experience of universal significance for understanding the new era, and to promote the flourishing of intellectual, academic and cultural life in its own country. The Study Group’s first major undertaking after its founding was to edit and publish Paths to Xi Jinping Thought: Memoirs of Long-Standing Friends of China and Solidarity Activists . Published in 2023, it is a collection of memoirs by international friends and senior figures in friendship organisations who have long worked for friendship with China and firmly supported its development.
The authors draw on their own experience to review their history of engagement with China. They bear vivid witness to China’s leap forward in the new era. On that basis they explain how they understand and identify with the formation of Xi Jinping Thought and its practical power.
The book offers the distinctive observations of overseas eyewitnesses, stepping outside the usual perspectives of domestic research. It shows the far-reaching influence of Xi Jinping Thought in three areas: guiding China’s development, promoting friendship and mutual trust between China and other countries, and helping to build a community with a shared future for mankind. It also shows how this thought is being spread and recognised ever more widely in the international community.
In the book’s Preface, Keith Bennett writes:
“Today the socialist countries are the collective leading force of the international working class and progressive movement. In terms of global reach and explanatory power, Xi Jinping Thought is the most influential body of thought among these countries. British socialists, like their comrades around the world, should therefore find effective ways to guide progressive people to study and deeply understand this valuable intellectual resource. Accomplishing this task means confronting many unresolved questions. We have long felt that how to make revolution in Western Europe remains an unanswered question, and for decades since we have been searching for the answer.” [1]
Bennett regards the book as an important contribution to that search. It collects the personal experiences and reflections of some long-standing friends of China. Over several decades these people have followed varied and complex political and intellectual paths, yet each in their own way confirms that “Xi Jinping Thought has universal applicability to the great task of uniting socialists and other progressive people and arming them ideologically.” [2]
Compiling the book took hundreds of hours of collaborative work. This included in-person meetings, in-depth interviews and thematic seminars, as well as telephone and online meetings during the Covid-19 pandemic. The process produced a large body of recordings and transcripts, which give a solid basis for further research. The main pieces in the book include “China Under Xi Jinping and the Anti-Imperialist Struggle of Our Time” and “China in the Xi Jinping Era and Communism”. Its main views are as follows:
(1) China now stands at the centre of the world stage. That reality alone should be reason enough for anyone who wants to understand the world rationally to study Xi Jinping Thought in depth. For socialists everywhere the need is more urgent still, in both theory and practice: Xi Jinping Thought offers invaluable practical experience and theoretical insight for the global socialist cause.
(2) Xi Jinping Thought is the guiding thought created and summed up by the Communist Party of China and its leaders. It has led China to great transformation and great achievements. It is now fully open to the peoples of the world, a great gift to all humanity. It can unite progressive forces worldwide, arm socialists and progressives ideologically, and encourage progressive people in the West to study the theory of socialism with Chinese characteristics in depth.

Microsoft's next-gen Xbox hardware lineup is beginning to come into focus. According to a new report from Fortune , the company is gearing up to ship new hardware in the form of a handheld in 2027, followed by a full-blown console in 2028.
It's unclear if the handheld project is a first party Xbox device, or a third-party device designed and manufactured by an OEM partner like ASUS and the ROG Ally X . The console is expected to be first-party, and is likely to run a specialized version of Windows.
The report claims that Xbox and Windows have been at odds about how the OS should run on Project Helix. Windows leaders wanted the consoles to run a modified version of Windows desktop, but Xbox leaders wanted a more boutique OS experience designed for gaming.
"Tensions ran high enough that a senior Xbox executive threatened to scrap the handheld project rather than adopt the Windows build ... Xbox is now largely controlling the direction of the operating system for the project" Fortune claims.
Windows already powers the current Xbox Series consoles, as well as Xbox One. It's a modified version of the OS that the Xbox team has customized, built on top of the Windows OS core that is developed by the Windows team. It sounds like the Xbox team has decided to maintain this approach with Project Helix consoles.
Alarmingly, Fortune claims that Microsoft is currently expecting the next-gen Xbox console to cost somewhere between $1,200 and $1,800, making it the most expensive gaming console ever. It's possible that Microsoft may choose to subsidize the cost, which would bring it closer to $1,000, but nothing is confirmed.
Of course, these rumors are unconfirmed. Plans could change and schedules could slip, so nothing is set in stone until Microsoft is ready to formalize its plans officially. For now, we know that Project Helix is still in development, with first devkits expected to debut in early 2027.

King Charles III praised Oman's peacemaking attempts in the Middle East Tuesday as Sultan Haitham bin Tariq began the first state visit by an Omani ruler to the U.K. in nearly half a century.
Hailing longstanding diplomatic, military and royal ties at a Windsor Castle banquet, the British monarch paid tribute to Muscat's "noble efforts" to help reopen the choked Strait of Hormuz.
"I would especially like to recognize, at a time when conflict has returned so painfully to the region, Oman's enduring commitment as a trusted interlocutor to all parties," Charles told around 160 guests at the lavish dinner.
"Oman's role across the Gulf and her 'constructive neutrality' — as you put it — matters far beyond Hormuz, and is worthy of our utmost respect," Britain's king added in a toast to the Omani sultan.
The first state visit to Britain by a sultan of Oman for 44 years comes amid severe turbulence in the Middle East prompted by the U.S.-Iran war.
Oman, a key U.K. military ally which borders the vital Hormuz waterway, has acted as a mediator in talks between the U.S. and Iran since the conflict flared in late February.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth confirmed Tuesday that he visited Israel on Monday and met with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, saying he "was there visiting our troops" and "had a chance to talk to the prime minister."
The unannounced visit came just over a week before Netanyahu's party faces elections. It also comes after President Trump floated resuming military operations against Iran following next month's U.S. midterm elections.
"Of course, the nature of our conversations is not something I would talk about but they've been good partners and I appreciate that," Hegseth said of his meeting with Netanyahu.
U.S. diplomatic missions across the Middle East have issued a new round of security warnings to Americans amid escalating attacks by Iran-backed Houthi militants against Saudi Arabia, including an Oct. 10 strike on Riyadh's international airport that killed an American citizen.
The alerts, issued Sunday by U.S. embassies in Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and several other countries, warned that hostilities could rapidly and without warning spread beyond areas already affected by the fighting. The advisories urged Americans to exercise vigilance and prepare for possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and other travel disruptions.
"We are actively warning U.S. citizens about the very real threat the Houthis pose and urging them to heed official guidance," Edgar Vasquez, the State Department's deputy assistant secretary for press, told CBS News.
"These alerts are part of a proactive effort by the Trump administration to ensure Americans are aware of potential risks," Vasquez said, adding that the safety and security of American citizens remain the department's "top priority."
President Trump said the U.S. is "doing very well with Iran" and he's just deciding how he wants to win the war.
"As you know, we're doing very well with Iran," Mr. Trump said as he took questions from reporters in the Oval Office at an unrelated executive order signing. "We just have to make a final decision of which way do we want to win? Do we want to win the nice way or the not nice way? But we're doing very well."
The war, which Mr. Trump said would take only a few weeks in March, has now dragged on for almost eight months with no apparent end in sight. Iran said on Tuesday it would not return to the negotiating table unless the U.S. drops its sanctions, threats and pressure campaign — an unlikely demand.
The president also discussed Europe not helping the U.S. with the war with Iran, saying, "We don't need any help. But I was testing them."
"I just called individual presidents and prime ministers to ask, would they like to help us? And they said, 'No,'" Mr. Trump said. "I said, 'Well, that's not nice.' You know, we spend hundreds of billions a year on NATO. And they said no."
Iran is taking a hard-line stance on negotiations with the U.S. to end the war, with President Masoud Pezeshkian saying Tuesday there will be no return to talks without a halt to the pressure campaign by the U.S.
Pezeshkian met with representatives from Pakistan, including army chief Asim Munir, on Tuesday. Pakistan has played an integral role as a mediator in peace talks between the U.S. and Iran, including the brief success of the Islamabad Memorandum in June.
"(Pezeshkian) told Pakistan's Field Marshal Asim Munir that US warmongering lies behind regional tensions, including disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz," according to a readout of the meeting from the official Iranian government account on X . "He said Washington must lift its pressures, threats and sanctions before any negotiations."
Those conditions are unlikely to be agreed upon by the U.S., which has stepped up its sanctions , dubbed Operation Economic Outcast, over the past month. President Trump has said the economic pressure campaign has become the main strategy for ending the war.
Pezeshkian also met with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Tehran on Tuesday. Iran and Russia have become powerful allies.
Naval mines have halted three tankers attempting to travel the Strait of Hormuz via routes considered illegal by Tehran, Iranian Revolutionary Guards said on Tuesday.
"Two violating oil tankers were set ablaze and halted due to the explosion of mines planted by the brave sailors of the IRGC Navy at an illegal crossing point in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz," the Guards said in an earlier statement on their official Sepah News website.
The Guards later said in a statement carried by state TV that a third oil tanker "exploded and caught fire after striking a naval mine south of the Strait of Hormuz."
The tanker "carrying over 2 million barrels of crude oil, had deactivated all of its radar and navigation systems," the statement added.
Iranian forces have, since the outbreak of the Middle East war, repeatedly targeted ships attempting to pass through Hormuz via a southern, U.S.-approved route close to the Omani coast.
President Trump has said on several occasions that the Strait of Hormuz has been cleared of all mines.
Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, on Tuesday told visiting Pakistani army chief Asim Munir that Tehran will not allow nuclear material to leave the country, according to state TV.

"There will be no negotiations until America takes steps to build trust — a process that must begin with the fulfillment of Iran's conditions."
